name: One saturated accent on the narrated element
description: The frame sits in one muted, desaturated or single-hue family and exactly one element, the one the narration names in the current clause, carries a saturated hue. When the narration moves to a new subject the accent moves with it and the previous element is demoted back to the field family.
when_to_use: Every explanatory frame in every style of the corpus: it tells the learner where to look without arrows or labels, and matters most in busy places, crowds and multi-part diagrams where only one part is being discussed.
how_to_execute: Build the shot in the muted field family first (muted earth, sage, teal, cool grey or one warm monochrome).
Reserve one accent hue the field does not contain (often red, yellow, coral or a cool blue), usually from the opposite temperature.
Give the accent only to the element named in the current clause; keep moving props and secondary figures in the field family.
If the accent is itself the event (a flag rising, a coin appearing), hold it back until the keyword.
When the subject changes, move the accent to the new element and remove it from the old one rather than adding a second.
When two things are compared, give each side its own accent and nothing else; optionally dim the rest with a translucent wash.
timing: Persistent through each shot; accent moves observed at colour_change medians of 0.6 to 1.1 s across batches. Batch counts: colour accent was the focal cue in 214 of 640 shots (batch 01) and 375 of 1003 (batch 08).
loom_notes: Packs carry an accent token, but nothing binds it to the narrated element or checks it. Needs a per-beat accent target in the storyboard and a frame check that counts saturated hue clusters per frame and flags a second accent that is not part of a declared colour-coded pair.

name: One small ambient loop keeps every hold alive
description: On a held frame the subject and camera stay still while one small, slow, low-contrast loop (rain streaks, drifting specks, smoke, flame flicker, steam, a sway, a blink, a slowly turning ring) keeps the frame from freezing without competing with the content.
when_to_use: Every hold longer than about 2 to 3 s: diagrams being read, portraits, establishing shots, emotional and philosophical beats, term cards, end cards.
how_to_execute: Choose one, at most two, ambient elements native to the scene and matching its meaning (rain for dread, petals for ceremony, confetti for payoff).
Start the loop before the hold so it does not pop on.
Loop it slowly and seamlessly at low amplitude and quiet colour; let the longest elements carry the most sway.
Keep it off the focal subject; it is never the brightest, fastest or accent-coloured thing in the frame.
Freeze the subject in a clear pose and let at most one gesture land on the narration.
Thin or stop the loop when a new focal element arrives.
timing: Ambient loop medians 3.0 to 5.2 s across the eight batches (p25 about 1.6 to 2.75 s, p90 7.8 to 10.4 s); secondary motion medians 0.29 to 0.5 s.
loom_notes: Ambient drift and particles exist and should stay seeded and slow. Missing presets: rain streaks and doodle wobble; hand-drawn line boil is on the not-possible list. The code counts grain boil and compression jitter as motion, so per-film motion-share figures do not measure this technique.

name: Credits in a black bottom bar over a held final image
description: The film ends on one calm, sparse final image (a tableau, a map with a tiny traveller, a procession, the opening studio) that holds with only small ambient or character loops while a thin solid black bar of credits sits along the bottom; the picture never cuts away to a separate credits card.
when_to_use: Every lesson end: close on a calm, readable image while credits, source notes or citations run.
how_to_execute: Compose one graphic final image with a single accent and large negative space; keep the upper field free of new ideas.
Animate only small loops: blinks, tail flicks, slow drift, a looping procession.
Slide a solid black bar up from the bottom edge and fix it.
Set credits small and white, as role-over-name pairs, rolling or swapped in two or three blocks by hard cuts or slides.
Keep the logo and picture above the bar fixed so the eye stays anchored.
Hold for the length of the credits.
timing: Credits run about 6 to 20 s across the films (most 8 to 19 s); credit text height median 0.03 of frame (p90 0.05, code).
loom_notes: Recap, title and end templates exist as text cards; a credits bar over the live last station (bar height, roll speed or block timing) is a template variant to add. Credit text at 0.03 of frame height sits on the reading floor; check it at 1080p. Batch 05 did not record this as a separate technique, so 84 is a floor, not a ceiling.

name: The picture changes on the word that names it
description: Every new element (label, icon, figure, number, prop) enters as its naming word is spoken, and each shot's one main visual event (a morph, a landing, a break, a glow, a gesture) completes or peaks on the key word that names the result, so picture and word confirm each other. Nothing appears before it is named.
when_to_use: Always: every beat, every list item, every diagram part, every cause-and-effect result. It is the main tie between picture and narration across the corpus.
how_to_execute: Mark the naming word or result word of each beat in the script.
Read its time from word-level narration timings, never from fixed times.
Map one element or one visual change to each marked word; do not stack two changes on one word.
Start an entrance so it settles on the word; schedule a transformation so its end or peak, not its start, falls on the word.
Place labels beside, never over, the face or subject they name.
Hold what is already shown, and hold a new state at least about a second after its word while the sentence continues.
Check on a frame strip that each landing frame sits on its word.
timing: Entrances are short: pop-in medians 0.4 to 0.58 s across batches (p25 about 0.3 s, p75 up to 1.38 s), scale-in 0.67 to 0.88 s, slide-in 0.75 s, fade-in 0.5 to 0.7 s; morph and transform-into medians about 1.0 to 1.3 s. The vision model labelled the large majority of shots as picture and word coinciding and described entries starting slightly ahead of the word. That is the model's description, not a measurement (its offset field reads 0.0 for nearly every shot), so no offset value is given here; set any lead by eye on the strip.
loom_notes: Cue resolution from Kokoro word timings exists. Still to add: a gate that fails any element shown before its word and any key word with no visual event; confirm in code whether a cue can anchor the end or peak of a change rather than its start, and expose a lead value to tune by eye.

name: Silent brand card dissolving into a quote card
description: The film opens with no voice on a near-white field: a centred wordmark with one saturated accent holds, cross-dissolves on the same axis into a centred one or two line quote in thin type with a much smaller attribution, then hands off to the first scene. The quote names the film's theme, tension or paradox before any picture or term.
when_to_use: Any lesson opener that should set a calm, credible, editorial register and pose the central tension in one line before content starts.
how_to_execute: Hold the brand mark centred on a near-white field for about 1 to 2 s, with one saturated accent on the mark only and heavy negative space.
Cross-dissolve (not a hard cut) to the quote card on the same field and centre axis.
Set the quote light and smaller than the mark, about 0.05 to 0.10 of frame height (median about 0.07); set the attribution much smaller again below it so hierarchy comes from size, not colour.
Hold the quote with zero motion long enough to be read; keep the card silent and let music carry it.
Optionally fade a faint, low-contrast version of the first scene in behind the text over the last 1 to 2 s (see card_to_scene_fade_up).
Hand off to the first scene at about 6 s and start the narration only after the cards.
timing: The card shot spans 0 to about 6.0 s in most films (6.0 to 6.8 s; 10.4 s in one film that adds a year stamp and a character card); the wordmark holds about 1 to 1.2 s before the dissolve; first spoken word at about 6 to 8.7 s in most films (code word timings), with a few outliers near 12 to 13.7 s; brand title about 0.15 to 0.20 of frame height on the brand beat.
loom_notes: Title and quote templates plus a fade or dissolve join cover it; keep the hold silent. The quote must be a real, sourced quotation grounded in the source (never an invented attribution), and the client's own brand mark replaces the channel mark; any hatch fill inside the mark is a brand asset, not a pack effect.

name: Zoom through a portal shape into the next scene
description: The camera pushes into an aperture that already exists in the outgoing frame (a monitor, a doorway, a letter's counter, a map pin or dot, an eye, a mouth, a liquid surface, a cell boundary, a comic burst) until it fills the frame and becomes the next scene, so the change reads as travel through one continuous space and the join means 'into'.
when_to_use: Changes of scale or register: outside to inside, system to part, body to cell, map to place, photo to memory, set to presenter, device to its content.
how_to_execute: Place the portal object in the outgoing frame before the move starts, usually centred where the eye already is, and give it the accent so the eye locks on it.
Push in on one axis with an ease-in so the move accelerates into the opening; let surrounding elements fade or leave frame.
Carry the field or line colour, or particles, through the join so the eye keeps the thread; add a brief flash only if the two spaces differ a lot.
Swap to the incoming scene while the aperture rim is still outside the frame so no seam shows.
Open the new scene inside the portal outline in the same line language, already centred on its subject, and settle with a short ease-out.
Name the term or drop an anchor character into the new field as the scale settles; optionally pull back out through the same shape later to close the loop.
timing: Portal shots are usually short, about 0.6 to 3.6 s (ease-in moves median about 0.8 s); slow dives such as organ to cell run up to about 7 to 14 s.
loom_notes: The zoom join with the 'into' meaning and nested child stations exist. Missing parameters: a portal mask in an arbitrary shape (letterform, eye, head, burst), and colour-locking the portal's fill across the join. The storyboard must name the portal object explicitly.

name: Locked camera by default; one move with one meaning when it moves
description: The frame is locked in most shots and the motion budget goes to the content: morphs, stamps, draw-ons, particles, gestures and ambient loops supply all the movement, and rhythm comes from cuts and shot-size changes. When the camera does move, it is one slow move with one meaning (push in to emphasise or enter, pull out to reveal scale, tilt to reveal a destination, truck to follow a route), never coverage and never compound.
when_to_use: Default for every explanatory, diagram and character shot; reserve lens moves for reveals, entries, descents and scale changes.
how_to_execute: Compose each shot to read without a move and lock the camera.
Give every beat one meaningful in-frame change, carried by an element or a gesture.
On long holds add an ambient loop instead of a camera drift.
Vary shot size between cuts (wide, medium, close, full-frame diagram) for rhythm.
Allow a move only when it reveals, changes scale, enters a space or follows a path; decide its meaning first.
Use one move per shot and time its end to the spoken word it reveals.
timing: Static camera in about 0.8 of shot records in the four batches that counted it (512 of 640, 529 of 621, 546 of 702, 815 of 945); per-film motion share still high (about 0.59 to 0.98). Eased camera moves: ease-in-out median about 0.4 s, ease-out about 0.75 s, ease-in about 0.83 s; reveals in the records run 1 to 9 s.
loom_notes: Static is Loom's default camera and the design seed and AI-tells lint already check camera habit; push, pull, pan and camera-on-element cover the allowed moves. Camera labels are among the most self-consistent fields (0.88 agreement), so this pattern is well supported.

name: One paper, grain or texture finish over everything
description: One fine paper grain, film grain, noise, stipple, crayon, watercolour, halftone or cracked-paint finish sits over every fill and layer, backgrounds, diagrams and inserts included, often with a soft darkening edge vignette, so flat vector, 3D and type read as one printed or hand-made material and hard cuts read like pages of one sketchbook.
when_to_use: Every editorial, storybook, sketch or textured flat style; films that mix 2D, 3D and photo; flat noir that would otherwise look like a sterile digital void.
how_to_execute: Choose one ground and one texture for the whole film.
Apply it uniformly at constant strength over every scene and layer, including diagrams, maps and 3D inserts; change palette by segment, never the ground.
Keep it fine enough that foreground outlines and text stay crisp (some films keep text clear of it).
Optionally add a soft corner or radial vignette, especially on parchment or cream fields.
Use halftone dots in shadow areas or scratches on artefact panels only where the style calls for it.
Judge the strength on the encoded MP4, not the source frame, so it survives compression.
timing: Constant across the film. Texture coded paper in 212 shots across 10 films of one batch; another batch coded texture none in 456 of 1003 shots, so the finish is common but not universal.
loom_notes: Paper and grain finishes exist in the shader layer but are kept near off by default; these films run them visibly. Needs a film-wide finish-strength setting judged on the encoded MP4; halftone, stipple and cracked-paint textures are not finish options yet (assets).

name: Pull back from one detail to reveal scale or context
description: One continuous pull-out starts tight on a highlighted unit or ambiguous detail (a tile, a rack, a figure, a child on a rope, a flat bar) and reveals it as one of many, or as the surface of something larger (a fleet, a lattice, a crowd, a city, a globe); the subjects hold still so the wide reads as a reframe of the same world, not a new scene, often with a tiny human for scale.
when_to_use: Scale and context: one case to a population, a local event becoming system-wide, showing one part as a piece of a larger system, surprise reframes, emotional payoffs.
how_to_execute: Open tight on one readable, highlighted detail and hold long enough for it to be understood.
Pull back slowly in one continuous eased move on one axis; keep hero elements in place.
Let other units or new elements enter at the frame edges, staggered on their words, as the frame widens.
Flatten receding figures into silhouettes and add a small human reference.
Land the widest frame on the key spoken word, then hold the wide for the idea to sit.
timing: Reveal shots run about 0.8 to 18 s (fast reveals 0.8 to 1.4 s; slow pulls 4 to 13 s, one continuous pull of 11.4 s); ease-out moves median about 0.9 s (p90 4.8 s). Pull-out is tagged in every batch.
loom_notes: The pull move exists and seeded arrays give the copies; the larger object must be built around the close view in the same station. A flat-to-3D reveal needs a three.js clip.

name: Frame within the frame
description: An aperture native to the world (doorway, window, arch, mirror, monitor, magnifier rim, gilt frame, coin, scroll, car mirror, foliage) frames the subject, isolating it, marking it as observed, reported or entered, or hosting another world inside this one. The content inside can change while the surround stays still, and an inset lens can follow a moving subject.
when_to_use: Thresholds and arrivals, points of view, quoted evidence or a backstory, memories, the boundary between two domains, singling one item out of a crowd, authority behind a barrier.
how_to_execute: Pick a frame object native to the world and draw it darker, plainer or heavier than its content.
Darken or desaturate everything outside the frame; place the subject inside at the brightest value, often backlit.
Hold the frame steady; move the subject, push in, or time the arrival through it on the key phrase.
To change the idea, swap the content inside the aperture (cross-dissolve, fill an empty slot, saturate on arrival).
Optionally zoom out to reveal the frame and recontextualise the shot.
Reuse the same frame motif later to bookend or re-anchor the boundary.
timing: Static device held for the whole shot (shots of 1.4 to 9.6 s); an arrival in a doorway observed landing on the spoken name in a 3.0 s shot; a following lens moves with path-follow (median 1.7 s). Tagged in 30 and 42 shots across 9 and 8 films of two batches.
loom_notes: Camera on one element, iris joins, masks and place props (doorway, window, monitor) cover a drawn frame. Missing: an aperture that hosts a separate station inside it, and a camera-on-element inset lens. Content cross-dissolves inside the aperture may trip Loom's double-exposure check; treat that as a gate conflict to resolve, not a defect of the films.

name: Slow push-in that lands on the named subject
description: A slow push-in over a held picture isolates one subject from a busy field, tightens on a face or symbol, and arrives as the key word or name is spoken, adding weight without adding information; a label may land once the object fills the frame, a very slow push on a nearly still figure builds unease or inward focus, and a sub-second push makes a reaction punch.
when_to_use: Emphasising one element of a held scene, naming one item among many, introducing a protagonist, building tension before a reveal, a legacy line or an inward turn.
how_to_execute: Hold the composition with the target already present; start wide enough to show the context.
Keep the frame static until just before the noun, then start the push.
Push on one axis only, eased, toward the focal subject; keep the subject nearly still.
Time the end of the push to the name or key word, then hold on it once framed.
Land a label on the object once it fills the frame if it must be named.
For a reaction beat, compress the push to under a second on a held face.
timing: Push-ins sit in shots of about 1 to 15 s, with very slow tension pushes of 9 to 17.6 s; a single-out push about 1 s; a reaction push 0.6 s. Push-in is tagged in 40 to 57 shots per batch and is the most common move in several batches.
loom_notes: Push move and camera-on-element exist; bind the push's end time to a word timing.

name: Music alone carries the branded open, credits and wordless beats
description: The film opens on the brand mark and a quote or title card with no speech; the music bed carries those first seconds, the narrator's first word lands after the card, on or after the first picture, and music alone returns under the credits and any wordless release beat.
when_to_use: Every film open and close, cold opens and emotional pauses; it sets a calm, premium register before content.
how_to_execute: Start the music bed at frame 0 under the brand and quote card.
Hold narration until the card ends; fade up the first scene, then start the voice on or after the first picture.
Duck the bed under the first word and keep it ducked while narration runs.
Mark no-speech shots in the timeline and let the music come up in them.
Raise the bed again under the credits.
timing: First word at about 6.3 to 8.1 s in every film of the batches that measured it (batch 01: ten films at 6.5 to 7.3 s and one at 16.05 s; batches 05 and 06: all 12 films each); code bed level a median 5.6 to 6.8 dB below speech while the voice runs. Batch 08 tagged 56 of 1003 shots as no speech.
loom_notes: Music by mood with ducking and a narration start offset exist; the open and credits gaps must be authored in the timeline. No sound records were made in this study, so these come from the code's film-level audio numbers; the evidence shots are opening and closing shots, not sound measurements.

name: Hold at anchors, cut fast through lists
description: Rhythm follows meaning, not a fixed shot length: the film slows to long, nearly still holds at definitions, key lines, results, data builds and diagrams, and speeds to short shots through lists, alarms and examples, then returns to a hold.
when_to_use: Every lesson. The burst serves listing and urgency, the hold serves understanding; diagrams with more than one step or layer get the longest shots.
how_to_execute: Mark each script section as anchor (definition, result, diagram, mechanism, emotional beat) or as list or alarm.
Compose each anchor picture so it is complete before its line starts.
Hold the anchor for the full sentence plus a beat, with a static camera; limit motion to the build itself plus one ambient loop.
Cut list and alarm items on each item's word, at about 1 to 4 s per shot.
Return to a long hold after every montage.
Never run two long builds back to back without a short human or punctuation beat between them.
timing: Shot length batch medians 4.2 to 5.0 s (p25 2.4 to 2.6 s, p75 8.2 to 10.4 s, p90 8.4 to 14.8 s); cuts per minute batch medians 8.46 to 9.7. Diagram and build shots run about 10 to 18 s (bVjKL1zd-vQ s028 15.8 s, v27fd0fa271 s047 18.2 s, uBwkMc1llmM s014 17.8 s). Over the whole corpus the code finds the longest still stretch per film at median 5 s and maximum 24 s, with 10 of 96 films holding over 10 s; the batch figures for longest hold were computed on truncated input and are superseded by these.
loom_notes: The timeline can do it and holds are authored in the storyboard. Missing: a pacing gate keyed to section type (lists allowed short, diagrams allowed long), and static-hold lints must not flag a deliberate hold that carries ambient life. The judge model often condemns such holds as static_hold; treat that as a known false alarm.

name: The previous subject morphs into the next subject
description: One isolated shape carries the idea into the next shot: its outline and fill interpolate into the next subject (a circle into a hub node, a metronome into a heart, a seed into an eye, a crowd into one worker, a date label into a coin), so the join is a change rather than a cut and the change itself explains the link.
when_to_use: Causal, combining or transformational ideas where a cut would break the link: one thing becoming another, two things merging, the next idea literally growing from the last.
how_to_execute: End the outgoing shot with one isolated object at a known position on a plain field, held still and readable.
Keep its position, scale and one shared colour or stroke constant through the change so the eye stays on it.
Interpolate its outline and fill toward the target in one continuous move.
Land the end state on the word that names the new idea; mark it with a small glow, halo or burst if needed.
Hold briefly so the new meaning settles, then build the rest of the new scene around it.
timing: Morph motions median about 0.7 to 1.5 s across batches (p90 2.7 to 5.3 s); transform-into median 0.7 to 1.0 s.
loom_notes: The continue join and hold-and-transform (lift, heat, peel) exist, but outline-to-outline path interpolation between two different SVG shapes is missing; simple vector path morphs are buildable in code, organic hand-drawn morphs are not possible. Until then, design both ends to share an outline.

name: Colour script: one dominant field per section
description: Each narrative section or chapter gets its own dominant field colour (and mood pair) while the accent rule, type, cards and drawing language stay constant, so the palette itself chapters the film without title cards. Some films darken the field step by step through a descent, or turn warm interiors cold at an emotional turn.
when_to_use: Films with distinct chapters (problem, mechanism, limits, future), multi-stage processes, descents in depth or scale, and emotional turns.
how_to_execute: Write a colour script before building shots: one dominant field (plus mood) per section.
Keep the field fixed within a section; never change it inside one idea.
Keep the accent hue and its role constant across all fields.
Change the field at the section boundary with a wipe, scale-to-fill, collapse, dissolve or cut.
For a descent, darken the vertical gradient one step per beat.
Return to the opening palette or a brand neutral for the close.
timing: Sections in these records run roughly 10 to 70 s each (one colour script: 15 to 50 s per hue; another 22.6 to 73.6 s per segment); field swaps ride 0.6 to 1.0 s wipes.
loom_notes: Packs fix one palette per lesson. Needs a per-section field override in the storyboard (or the design seed assigning station field hues from the pack) while the accent token stays fixed.

name: A flat hand enters from the frame edge to act
description: A single simplified hand, with no arm or body, enters from the nearest frame edge on the action word, performs one action on the composition (place, present, pick, remove, tick, draw, turn a dial, stamp) and leaves the way it came, so the result holds alone. At large scale the same hand stands for an outside force: an institution, a policy or support that lifts, cradles or removes small figures.
when_to_use: Any simple human action on a diagram or still life where a full character would distract: choosing one option, removing one unit, presenting evidence, ticking a checklist, building step by step, or showing a system acting on people.
how_to_execute: Compose the objects first as a still life, a row or a diagram and hold it.
Enter the hand from the nearest frame edge, often on a diagonal, on the spoken action word.
Perform exactly one action with an ease-out (grab, place, lift, tick, press, sweep); for a repeated process, repeat one two-beat gesture per step.
Hold a beat after the action so the change settles.
Exit the same way it entered, leaving the frame clean for the next idea.
Draw the hand in the figure outline weight of the pack, untextured, so it reads against a textured world.
For an outside force, scale the hand far above the figures and act once on the keyword, or reveal it in a pull-back as the ground the scene stands on.
timing: slide_in median 0.67 to 0.79 s and exit_slide median 0.79 to 0.83 s (code, per batch); a hand beat fills 2 to 13.6 s shots; a quick helper hand can enter and exit in under 0.5 s; a two-hand clasp eases out over about 4 s and holds.
loom_notes: Checked by grep: runtime/objects.js has no hand object (its 'hand' hits are clock hands), and the capability list names none. Loom needs a hand prop family per pack (open, point, grip, pinch, press, tick) with a prop socket, entry and exit from a named frame edge, and an outline weight taken from the pack. A cursor exists for UI scenes and is the nearest substitute. Suits a corporate audience well: it shows agency without casting a person.

name: Split screen or equal panels for comparison
description: Two, three or four equal panels divided by a thin seam, gutter or hard edge show the same subject at identical scale and orientation, so the one variable that differs is the only difference. Variants hold one panel constant while the other cycles examples, or show two simultaneous events (a diagonal seam for action).
when_to_use: A/B comparisons, before and after, control versus modified, two conditions in a study, cause and reaction at once, parallel events, members of one category.
how_to_execute: Divide the frame into equal panels with one clean seam (straight for comparisons, diagonal for action), often in the accent.
Mirror the layout and use identical figure scale and pose in each panel.
Change only one property per panel (colour, state, a symbol, the difference prop); tint each panel's field differently.
Bring panels in by a hard cut or a wipe of the second panel or divider, in reading order, cause first.
Land one label per side only after the split settles, left then right.
Optionally hold one panel constant as the reference while the other cycles on the spoken list, or grow from two panels to three when the line needs it.
timing: Split shots 0.8 to 19 s, most 3 to 12 s; split_screen tagged in 17 shots across 8 films and 20 shots across 6 films of two batches; one triptych held 5.6 s across three shots.
loom_notes: Split layouts are buildable in scene code and the icon grid template exists for text, but there is no split or grid layout parameter in the capability list: needs a panel-layout parameter that enforces identical scale, plus constant-and-cycling and growing-split variants.

name: Hard cut on the narration beat; gradual joins only for meaning
description: Most joins are hard cuts placed on a clause boundary or key word, the incoming shot already complete at its first frame; a change of speaker is a hard cut to a new close-up and a wide-to-close cut lands a punchline. Wipes, fades, morphs and dives are spent only on a change of world, scale, time or idea, which keeps them meaningful.
when_to_use: Default join grammar for every lesson, between ideas, examples or speakers in the same world when nothing carries over.
how_to_execute: Split the narration into clauses from the word timings.
End each shot on a clause boundary and cut on the first word of the next clause.
Make the incoming frame complete at its first frame so the cut reads instantly.
Change shot size across the cut for rhythm; cut to a close-up to flag a new speaker.
Carry the field colour, a diagonal or the accent across the cut so it reads as the same world.
Switch to a gradual or object-carrying join only when world, scale, time or chapter changes (into, time, era, meanwhile, shock).
timing: Code cut rate per film about 6 to 21 cuts per minute (one batch median 8.3, another 12.5); shot records median about 3.2 s (p10 1.0 s, p90 9.8 s), per-film medians mostly 2.8 to 4.6 s. Hard cuts are the large majority of labelled joins in every batch that counted them.
loom_notes: The cut join on word timings exists, and Loom joins already carry meanings (into, time, era, meanwhile, shock); the rule is to default to the cut and spend gradual joins only on those meanings. A clause-aligned cut placer is the only logic needed. Batch join counts may include sub-shot boundaries, so use the code cut rate, not join counts.

name: Voice-led mix: low bed, sparse effect hits
description: The music bed sits a few decibels under the voice throughout and non-speech hits are sparse; only about a third of cuts land on a hit, so sound punctuates stamps, reveals and scene turns rather than scoring every move.
when_to_use: Every narrated lesson's mix and effects pass.
how_to_execute: Duck the bed to sit about 6 dB under speech throughout.
Place hits only on stamps, reveals, impacts and scene turns that carry an idea.
Leave most cuts unaccented; aim for about a third of cuts on a hit.
Keep the bed continuous under transitions.
Cap non-speech hits at roughly 5 to 7 per minute.
timing: Code, film level: bed median 5.6 to 6.0 dB below speech in these batches (p10 2.8 to 4.0, p90 7.4 to 9.0); non-speech hits median 5.3 to 7.0 per minute (p10 4.1, p90 9.4 in batch 01); share of cuts on a hit, batch medians 0.333 to 0.367.
loom_notes: Ducked music and synthesised effects placed by the motion exist. Missing: a per-minute hit density cap and a share-of-cuts target, so motion-placed effects do not fire on every move. There are no per-shot sound records; the evidence shots are where the records describe a punctuating event.

name: Minimal faces, emotion carried by posture
description: People are drawn as types: dot eyes and one mouth line, a blank face or a few flat planes, and often simpler than the world they stand in (pictogram, stick or dot figures). Identity comes from clothing colour and silhouette; emotion comes from posture (upright, hunched, slumped, hands to head) and one head or hand gesture, not from facial acting.
when_to_use: Every illustrated character beat, especially for adult audiences: generic employees, groups and case-study people the viewer should project onto, and effort at system or landscape scale.
how_to_execute: Design faces with two dots and one curve, nothing, or a few flat planes.
Give each role one clothing colour so identity reads without a face.
Design three or four strong silhouettes per character (upright, hunched, slumped, open).
Switch pose on the narration beat; avoid continuous acting.
Isolate the person who matters with the accent colour or contrast.
When the world is the subject, draw people one line weight simpler than the environment and fade them out when focus returns to it.
timing: character_act median 0.5 to 1.0 s across batches (p25 0.29 to 0.46 s, p75 1.29 to 2.13 s; code); characters per shot median 1, p90 4; held-pose shots run 3 to 14.8 s with near-zero motion.
loom_notes: Rigs with poses, gestures and blinks exist and fit this restrained acting; complex body acting is weak in Loom, which this style does not need. Checked by grep: runtime/rigs/beans.js draws dot eyes and runtime/rigs/people.js has a swappable face layer, but a pack-level face mode (blank or dot eyes, lip sync off) was not found, so it is a parameter to add (not verified beyond the grep). Corporate packs avoid bean figures; pictogram or line figures fit engineering and line-art registers.

name: Close by returning to the opening image, changed
description: The closing shot returns to the opening set, subject, palette or motif (the studio monitor now cycling every speaker, the ship now carrying a new load toward a bright horizon, the first gesture seen from the other side), changed by what was learned, so the lesson reads as a resolved loop.
when_to_use: Lessons with a clear arc, story-led lessons and series formats; the closing beat before or under the credits signals completion and shows what changed.
how_to_execute: Plan the opening image as the closing image from the start; plant a distinctive image in the first 30 s.
Return to it in the last 10 to 30 s with a cut or dissolve.
Change one thing that carries the conclusion: the load, the light, the company, the screen content, the pose; optionally reverse roles or perspective.
Resolve the opening question or peril inside it; warm the palette and slow the pace.
Hold it under the credits bar.
timing: Final holds of about 9 to 20 s including credits; the callback sits in the last 10 to 30 s.
loom_notes: Reusing a station by id is trivial in Loom; the director skill can require a planted opening image and a changed state for it at the close.

name: Label on the object, arriving with its word and clearing after
description: A short label (one or two words) sits on or right beside the part, region, species, person or place it names, with at most one thin leader line or short arrow, never in a caption bar or legend. It pops or fades in as the word is spoken and clears before the next clause, keeping the frame clean.
when_to_use: Naming parts of a structure, zones of a map or diagram, steps of a process, species, people, places and new terms.
how_to_execute: Show the picture first so the name lands on an understood image.
Attach the label inside or on the named object, or at the end of one leader line drawn to the exact part.
Use a small sans, typewriter caps or the film's hand style at about 0.05 of frame height (never under about 0.03); add a backing band if the ground is busy.
Pop, fade or draw it in on the spoken word in a contrasting accent.
Hold through the clause; fade it out before the next label appears.
For a key phrase, write it on word by word along the action's path.
timing: pop_in median 0.5 s, fade_in median 0.54 s, exit_fade median 0.38 to 0.7 s; label text height median 0.05 of frame (p10 0.03, p90 0.15).
loom_notes: Labels, measured text layout, pop and draw-on exist and Kokoro word timings allow exact cueing. Check the 0.03 reading floor at render size; label-inside-region anchoring and text along a path are parameters.

name: Slow lateral pan along a row, each item entering on its name
description: One slow horizontal pan or truck walks the eye along a row, wall, shelf, lineup, trail or long structure wider than the frame, so each item enters as the narrator names it and many reads without a cut per item; labels or data marks pop as items enter, and the move ends on the item that matters, often a contrasting or accent-coloured payoff.
when_to_use: Spoken lists, chronologies and version timelines, queues and bottlenecks, trails of evidence and pipelines, crowded scenes with one figure that matters.
how_to_execute: Lay the items out on one baseline or path wider than the frame, at the same scale.
Let the cut land and settle briefly, then start the pan from one end.
Move at a slow, steady, gently eased pace matched to the narration so each item centres near its word.
Pop each label, year or data mark as its item enters frame.
End on a differently scaled, isolated or accent-coloured item, or a foreground intruder, on the peak word.
timing: Pans and trucks of about 2 to 18 s (a card-wall pan across four shots totals 18.4 s; a timeline pan 4.6 s); pan right is among the most used moves.
loom_notes: Pan, truck and follow moves with parallax and staggered groups exist; binding each item's entry to its word time is the one piece of logic to add. Do not take 'constant speed' from these records as a rule: code-detected linear moves are measurement jitter.

name: A few linked worlds, each with one job
description: A film runs in two or a few visual worlds with fixed jobs (warm illustrated life scenes and a cool technical register; the room and the mind; a story world and an evidence desk; a hub studio or courtroom and its evidence vignettes; live speakers and flat art), each with its own palette and single accent, and crosses between them by a morph, zoom-through, glow handoff, carried object or a return to the hub, so variety never breaks coherence.
when_to_use: Lessons that mix narrative with mechanism, explain the mechanism behind an everyday experience, or need several registers (diagram, story, testimony); long chains of evidence.
how_to_execute: Give each world one job, one look and its own single accent; keep character design identical across worlds.
Write the world switches into the colour script; open each mechanism from a life moment.
Cross by a morph, zoom-through, glow handoff or a carried object, or a strong join (fade through black, white flash), not a bare cut.
Optionally define a hub set with fixed framing and return to it between worlds; let anchor characters react, not explain.
Place short, quiet human scenes (one gesture, a long hold) between long mechanism stretches to re-anchor stakes.
Return to the life register or the hub for the human payoff and the bookend.
timing: Crossings 1 to 2 s; anchor and human scenes 1.4 to 8 s; records list 7 to 10 colour-script segments per film with switches at segment joins; world consistency was 'few worlds linked' in 9 of 12 films of one batch.
loom_notes: Places, stations, joins and the cinema mix (two packs in one lesson) exist; the storyboard should record each world's job. Missing: a shared-element parameter to carry one object across a register join; courtroom and news-desk hub sets need assets.

name: Open on a concrete, relatable scene before any thesis
description: After the card, the first content is a situation, not an explanation: a named person, place or year with a problem, a queue at a gate, a hand reaching for an object, a parent waking a child. The concept or question emerges from the situation and is named only after the stakes are held.
when_to_use: Every lesson opening, and especially process or history lessons that risk reading as a spec sheet: give a human stake and a curiosity gap before vocabulary.
how_to_execute: Pick one moment the viewer has lived or can picture that already contains the problem.
Establish the place with a wide, mostly empty frame.
Cut or pull back to one figure; pop a name label or stamp a year on the spoken name or date.
Put the one accent on the object that will become the subject; show the problem as one gesture or object.
Run 3 to 13 short shots with no terms, then let the question emerge.
Name the concept only after the stakes are held.
timing: Establishing shots 3.8 to 10 s; seconds to first question in the records about 2 to 20 s in most films (median of one batch about 20 s), up to about 60 to 88 s in a few.
loom_notes: A storyboard choice; story-cartoon places, character rigs and text name labels support it. For corporate adults the scene should be a workplace moment, not a classroom one.

name: Bold term card stamped on the spoken term
description: A new term, code, question or principle keyword arrives alone and large (title height median 0.18 of frame) on one flat saturated field or over a held picture, often in a bold rounded or hand-lettered face with an outline or flat two-colour offset shadow, tilted or on a torn band; an object that embodies the term then surfaces under it or the word hands off to it. An acronym variant pops each letter on its own word.
when_to_use: The first time a term the learner must remember is spoken; section markers; the posed question; closing a thread with a category word. Never for sentences.
how_to_execute: Cut to a single saturated field, or hold the picture still so the word does not compete with motion.

Set one to five words large in a heavy display weight, optionally with an outline, a flat offset shadow, a slight tilt or a band or burst plate; split into a main and a smaller qualifier line when the speech has a hierarchy.
Stamp or pop it on the spoken term (scale from slightly larger, fast ease out).
Hold for the phrase, with at most a faint flicker or glow to keep the card alive.
Reveal a small figure or object that embodies the term, or morph the word into a prop.
Leave quickly: dim, slide off, push in or wipe into the explanation.
For an acronym, pop each letter on its word in its own accent and type the expansion beneath a thin rule.
timing: Cards hold 0.6 to 7 s, most 1.8 to 5.6 s; pop_in median 0.46 s; exit fade median 0.38 s; title height median 0.12 to 0.18 of frame (p75 0.22).
loom_notes: Title and definition templates and the stamp motion exist. Missing: hand-lettered and rounded display faces as pack fonts (licensed), flat offset-shadow, band and burst plates, the object-surfaces-under-term variant and per-letter acronym timing.

name: One recurring object threads the whole film
description: One object or mark central to the subject (a passport, a seed, a coin, a paper boat, a red thread, an egg, a potted plant, a family photo card, a costume mark, an element badge) is designed once with fixed colours and reused unchanged in every scene and world; it can travel, pile up as a countable unit, be carried by a hand across a join, or morph to carry the next idea.
when_to_use: Long histories or processes that need one anchor; lessons that follow one person, product, asset or record through a pipeline; binding many vignettes into one argument.
how_to_execute: Pick the object that is the lesson's subject, or one costume mark, at the start.
Design it once with one fixed colour (the accent or the darkest value) and a distinctive silhouette; never restyle it between shots.
Place it in each world and vignette where it applies, including the end.
Use it as the countable unit in piles and maps, or let it travel on carriers.
Carry it across joins by a hand or a slide where possible, or let it morph into the next idea.
Return to it for the payoff or recap.
timing: Whole film; carry moves follow path timing (median 1.63 s); one token appears at 9.4 s, 50.0 s and 278.0 s of one film.
loom_notes: Object grammars with families and states exist; the storyboard should declare the binding token so builders reuse it unchanged.

name: Cutaway that opens the hidden interior on the naming word
description: A sealed object, body, container or ground surface is opened (split, peeled, turned translucent or x-rayed, cut into a cross-section, or separated along one axis) exactly when the interior is named, so the hidden structure or process plays inside it; layers can be added one per spoken part over a constant reference line, or the cutaway is held while only one shape changes.
when_to_use: Anything hidden inside a system: internal structure, a stack of layers, steps users never see, slow or underground processes.
how_to_execute: Show the closed object or surface as one mass first.
Open it on the naming word: peel or split, tilt down through the ground, turn the fill translucent, cross-fade the body to a flat silhouette, or explode parts along one axis.
Draw the hidden band darker so pale elements read; reserve the accent for the active interior element.
Animate the contents in spoken order, or add one layer per named part over a constant reference line.
For slow mechanisms, hold the cutaway and change only one shape.
Use at most one leader line and a short label per part.
Close it, or swap back to the whole object, to link the diagram to the place.
timing: Cutaway shots 2.6 to 17.8 s; layer stacks build within about a second per named part in a 17.8 s shot; held one-change cross-sections 10.6 to 17.0 s; grow median 1.5 s, unfold median 1.29 s (code).
loom_notes: Unmask, peel, reveal, grow, depth-layered places and the inside-a-body place exist, and the iris join gives a lens mask. Missing: a cutaway or translucent state per object family, a layer-band template, an explode-along-axis parameter and a rig x-ray state. Long held cutaways are real here (holds up to 24 s occur in the corpus); Loom's still-beat and empty-frame checks should not fail them.

name: Tiny figure against a giant object or figure
description: A small whole human figure is placed against a vastly larger object, structure or cropped figure (a giant hand, ship, machine, tree, wall-sized circuit, billboard face, looming legs), so magnitude, burden or power imbalance reads without words or action.
when_to_use: Power imbalance, authority and threat, institutions versus individuals, burden, awe, the scale of a system relative to one person.
how_to_execute: Place the small figure low in the frame, drawn whole, often in the one warm accent so it still reads.
Let the giant element fill most of the frame in a simple shape, cropped at the frame edge so it feels larger than the frame.
Give the dominant element the accent instead if it is the threat.
Hold still, or keep the scene plain until the key word, then ignite or move the large element with a slow push-in or a pull-back reveal.
timing: Held 2 to 13.5 s; one slow push runs over a 12.2 s shot with the reveal timed to the keyword.
loom_notes: Composition only; depth layers, rig scaling and cropping, push and pull exist.

name: One subject lit by a glow or light pool in a dark void
description: A single symbolic object or subject sits in a near-black field, lifted by a soft radial glow, a spotlight cone or one warm light source (doorway glow, candle, lamp beam) instead of any environment or cast shadow; the light carries the change and fading it ends the beat.
when_to_use: Definitions, turning points and takeaways marked by one object; mechanisms that must be the only thing on screen; arrivals, discoveries, intimate, solemn or judgement beats; a person under scrutiny.
how_to_execute: Drop the scene to a dark void, often by a fade through black.
Place one light-toned subject, centred or on a third, kept small.
Put one soft radial glow, cone or warm shape behind or over it; keep the subject's brightest value inside the light.
Hold the subject still; animate only the glow (a slow pulse), a small wobble or faint drifting specks.
Write the label on as it is spoken, or swap small diagram elements in and out around the subject per idea.
Fade the light to end the beat.
timing: Holds of 0.6 to 12 s, most 2 to 9 s; bloom fade about 1.8 s; light_change medians 0.5 to 1.0 s; pop_in of swapped elements median 0.4 s.
loom_notes: Light pool, shader light and glow exist in cinematic-noir, dark-technical and glow-flat; a spotlight cone preset is a small addition. Replace stock icons with an object grammar.

name: Quantity as repeated identical units
description: A count, volume or frequency is shown by one small identical unit repeated in a row, grid, ring, stack or scatter whose density equals the quantity, often accumulating one by one until it reads as many, instead of an on-screen number or a chart; units reorganise or disappear to show change, and frequency can be one element cycling on a persistent object.
when_to_use: Large counts, populations, volume, frequency, growth and decrease, where the feel of 'a lot' matters more than the exact figure.
how_to_execute: Design one small unit that reads at tiny size; show one first.
Stagger more in, timed to the narration, in reading order on the spoken list.
Switch to smaller markers when the count grows past legibility.
Hold the full set static so the scale lands, or pull back to show the whole set.
Reorganise, remove or recolour units to show change; build the headline number from the same units if it must be stated.
For frequency, cycle one element on a persistent object and let the viewer count.
timing: pop_in median 0.4 to 0.5 s per unit (code); builds over 4 to 18 s shots; rise and fall cycles across a 13.8 s shot.
loom_notes: Unit grids, seeded arrays, staggered groups and loops exist. Every count must trace to the source, or be explicitly framed as illustrative.

name: Draw-on lines and marks as they are named
description: A line, crack, symbol, border, letter, calendar mark or annotation draws itself in real time as the narrator names it, so the picture is written as it is spoken.
when_to_use: Diagrams, symbols, terms, counts and annotations that should feel discovered; causes drawn before their consequences.
how_to_execute: Hold the ground.
Start the stroke on the spoken word.
Draw along the stroke's natural direction: reading order for letters, outward from the impact point for a crack.
Pace one stroke per spoken unit when counting; dashed lines may extend in short steps.
Taper the line end so it reads as drawn, not wiped.
Hold the finished drawing a beat before acting on it or moving to the next idea.
timing: Draw-on medians 0.67 to 0.75 s (p25 0.25 to 0.29 s, p75 1.3 to 1.5 s, p90 2.54 s); the finished fracture in 6hCo4S_1Fhw holds static over 1 s after drawing.
loom_notes: Draw-on and typewriter exist. Stepped dashed-line extension and tapered stroke ends are parameters to add.

name: A list builds one item per spoken name
description: A spoken list becomes a picture: empty slots are laid out, and units of one shape (seats, figures in a queue, emblems, checks, cards, petals of a crest) arrive one at a time in speech order and reading order, then the full set holds and clears together.
when_to_use: Any spoken list, roster, count, set of categories or process that fills a grid.
how_to_execute: Lay out empty slots for the whole set in reading order (row, grid, ring or arc).
Bring each unit in on its spoken word with a quick scale and small settle, so each gets its own beat.
Keep earlier units in place.
Keep every unit the same shape so only order and count carry meaning.
Hold the completed set for a beat so the eye can count it.
Clear the whole set together before the next idea.
timing: Pop-in medians 0.4 to 0.5 s (p25 0.25 s, p75 0.88 s, p90 1.84 s); slide-in median 0.63 s; in fast lists items arrive about one per second (nQf-lystVn4, 242 to 253 s).
loom_notes: Pop and staggered groups exist; drive the stagger from word timings, not a fixed interval.

name: One subject alone on a plain field
description: The set is dropped entirely: one subject, object or small one-to-two-figure vignette sits on a flat colour, smooth two-stop gradient or bare textured paper with medium to high negative space, grounded only by a soft shadow or one thin line, so the narration does the work and nothing competes.
when_to_use: Definitions, mechanism beats, single objects that carry a definition, step-by-step object changes, abstract ideas, feelings and list items that need one observable action rather than a place.
how_to_execute: Remove the environment; keep one flat or two-stop gradient field (vertical cool top to warm bottom, or a radial glow behind the subject).
Centre or slightly offset the subject; keep a vignette to one or two figures and one prop.
Ground it with a soft drop shadow, a flat offset shadow or one thin line, never a drawn floor.
Give it the frame's only saturated accent.
Transform or handle only that object, or add one small secondary motion (a blink, falling rain, an ambient loop).
Change the field colour between sections, not within a beat; swap to the next vignette by redraw or dissolve.
timing: Isolation shots run 1.4 to 16.7 s, most 2 to 6 s; secondary_motion median 0.46 s.
loom_notes: Presenter-pop, station backgrounds, gradients and object grammars with states cover it. Risk: a generic drawing reads as an icon slide; use an object grammar, not a stock icon.

name: Hand-lettered words written on as they are spoken
description: Labels, names, terms and questions are lettered in the art's own hand (brush, marker, chalk, casual script, wobbly double stroke, torn-paper cutout letters) and drawn on stroke by stroke as the word is spoken, sitting directly on the picture with no box, so they read as notes rather than captions.
when_to_use: Warm, human registers; naming a part, person, term, quantity or phenomenon inside a drawing; data points over textured backgrounds.
how_to_execute: Choose one hand-lettered face that matches the line weight of the art, plus one display contrast for key words.
Place the word near or on its object, not in a caption strip.
Draw it on stroke by stroke starting on the spoken word, often with a hand-drawn arrow.
Pair a small handwritten word with a large cutout word to weight the important term.
Remove it, cross it out or fade it before the next label so the frame stays sparse.
timing: draw_on median 0.75 to 1.08 s (p25 0.38, p75 2.5); label cap height median 0.05 of frame; stacked word cards hold about 2.5 s.
loom_notes: Draw-on, typewriter and word timings exist; fonts are pack data, so each sketch or warm pack needs a licensed hand-lettered face (ideally with stroke order for true write-on).

name: One gesture or pose change per shot, landed on the keyword
description: The body holds still with only blinks and small head shifts, and one action (an eye opening, a hand lift, a shrug, a point, an open palm, a salute) or one pose or expression change carries the whole shot, timed so its peak is on the stressed word. A secondary character may react a beat later.
when_to_use: Presenter and character beats where a person stands for the idea; any character moment that carries meaning.
how_to_execute: Pose the character and hold while the clause builds.
Find the stressed word in the line.
Anticipate slightly before it, then land the gesture or the new pose with an ease-out on the word.
Keep the camera static so the gesture is the only event.
Let a second character react a beat later if there is one.
Settle into a closed pose at the end of the thought.
timing: character_act median 0.5 to 1.0 s (p25 0.25 to 0.46 s, p75 1.8 to 2.04 s; code); lip_sync median 1.13 s. Landing on the word is the vision model's description, not a measured offset (sync_offset_s is a model field).
loom_notes: Rig gestures and poses can be cued to Kokoro word timings. A storyboard field naming the peak word per character beat would make the timing explicit.

name: Hold the frame and anchor, change the picture in place
description: Camera, ground and anchor subject stay put while the drawing around them changes: overlays pop in and clear, props are drawn out and the next ones drawn in, the background swaps, the pose changes. A chain of ideas reads as one continuous page rather than a set of scenes, and the viewer never has to find the subject again.
when_to_use: Several beats about the same subject, steps of one argument or process that should feel like a single thought, and lists of examples in sketchbook or line-art registers.
how_to_execute: Keep the background field, line weight and the anchor figure fixed in position and size.
Change only what the narration names, one thing per spoken beat: an overlay, a prop set, the background, a pose.
Fade or draw out the outgoing props while the incoming ones fade or draw in over about 0.5 to 1 s.
Clear the previous change before the next arrives; land the completed state on the keyword, then hold.
Cut only when the subject changes; use a short dissolve when jumping to a different source.
timing: Transform-into median about 1.0 s (p25 0.5 s, p75 1.9 s); vignettes turn over every few seconds; held-anchor shots run 10 to 17 s in testimony films.
loom_notes: The continue join, hold-and-transform and draw-on cover it for clean vector work; the wobbly hand-drawn redraw itself is not possible, so cross-fade whole vignette layers on a constant field. One film in this cluster (jLOuMXnM5wk) has no detected cuts, so its pacing is unknown and is not used here.

name: Quick-cut montage for lists and peaks
description: A spoken list, a chain of consequences, a time lapse or a climax becomes a run of very short locked-off shots, each one pose, action or vignette that reads instantly, against a backbone of longer shots.
when_to_use: Lists of examples, symptoms or cases, chains of cause and effect, time passing, building urgency or volume at a climax.
how_to_execute: Reduce each item to one pose, one action or one object.
Lock the camera and keep layout, line style, palette and subject position constant across the run; change one variable per cut.
Cut on each item's word or clause boundary, or use very short dissolves for a flip-book feel.
Use close-ups and frame-edge hands for threat rather than shown violence.
Run the burst for about 5 to 10 s at most.
Give the last item a longer build, or release with a dissolve or an empty beat, then return to a long hold.
timing: Shots of about 0.6 to 3.6 s, commonly near 1 s (NEFmWclWiOw s034 1.2 s; P8OEz3PvWZQ s014 to s018 about 1 s each); sub-second bursts at 0.6 to 1.0 s per cut (l29K-ZkARmE s040 to s043); flip-book dissolves 0.3 to 0.4 s (records).
loom_notes: Short beats, cuts and fades on word timings are supported. Missing: a storyboard list or burst group that keeps layout constant across its shots and tells the pacing gate these short shots are intended.

name: Wipe made of the material the story just named
description: The wipe edge is a material or shape already in the story (a snow mass, a blood drip, pipe smoke, a leaf, a cloud of hats, a starburst, a rising flood of the accent colour), grown from an element in the outgoing scene, so the scene change feels caused by the thing on screen and restates the topic.
when_to_use: Section changes and consequences where the threat or substance itself should end the scene; a rising flood for an overwhelming force or a new state taking over.
how_to_execute: Pick a material or shape the narration just named or the scene already shows.
Draw the wipe edge in that shape (drips, puffs, a crowd of objects, a snow wave); keep it irregular, never a straight line.
Grow or sweep it from an element of the outgoing scene, or raise it from the bottom edge as a flood, covering the subject fully.
Run it fast as punctuation and land it on the closing word of the sentence.
Reveal the next scene behind its trailing edge, or let it become the next field colour.
timing: Wipe-in median about 0.5 to 0.75 s (p75 1.4 to 2.4 s); punctuation wipes under about 1.4 s; floods run longer, up to several seconds (grow p90 3.6 s).
loom_notes: The wipe join exists as a geometric join; it needs a mask-shape parameter taken from the scene's subject (drip, puff cloud, object swarm, snow mass) and an accent-fill or colour-source parameter.

name: Hold an object, then turn it into its meaning
description: A plain object is held still, then transforms in place, without a cut, into what it means or into the next idea (a ticket into a tipping scale, steam into a skull, a box into a globe, a bust into the word it names), and the new form holds so the one change carries the point.
when_to_use: When two consecutive ideas share a subject, at thesis turns, and to make an abstract consequence or value concrete in one beat.
how_to_execute: Show the first form alone and still, long enough to read.
Keep field colour and line style constant.
Morph shape and colour together toward the second form on the keyword.
Land the completed form on the key phrase.
Add at most one settling secondary motion (a scale tilting and levelling).
Hold the new form still.
timing: Morph and transform-into medians 1.0 s (p25 0.6 to 0.7 s, p75 1.5 to 2.04 s); a slow ghost-to-reflection morph runs about 3 s (qLrnn24C3zU s058); 6hCo4S_1Fhw s011 is a 6.6 s shot with one morph and holds on both sides.
loom_notes: Hold-and-transform blueprints exist with lift, heat and peel; transforms between unrelated outlines need a shape-to-shape path morph primitive. Organic morphs are listed as weak.

name: Clear the stage before the next idea
description: Elements enter with eased moves and leave no slower than they came; overlays that belong to a sentence exit together at its end, so the anchor subject is readable again before the next idea arrives, and an exception is shown only on a cleared frame.
when_to_use: Every element move, especially dense explanations and held anchors (a face, a talking head, a map) that collect pop-in overlays.
how_to_execute: Enter with ease-out or ease-in-out.
Track which overlays belong to the current sentence.
Exit them together at the sentence end with a quick fade, scale-out or slide, no longer than the entry.
Let outgoing elements clear before incoming ones land.
Show exceptions only on a cleared frame.
timing: Entry medians (batch 04): pop-in 0.5 s, fade-in 0.7 s, slide-in 0.75 s, scale-in 0.88 s. Exit medians across batches: fade 0.46 to 0.7 s, slide 0.63 to 0.92 s, scale 0.42 to 0.63 s; in batch 04 exits ran faster than entries, so the safe rule is exits no longer than entries.
loom_notes: Loom's join grammar already makes outgoing elements leave first and exit motions exist. Missing: an automatic exit cue at the sentence end or next keyword, and exit durations matched to these medians.

name: Wipe edge drawn from the film's medium or recurring motif
description: One wipe shape per film comes from its own visual language: a ragged torn-paper edge whose back carries the outgoing colour, a page turn, a peeling seam of stitches, a scalloped cloud or tissue edge, a wavy two-colour boundary, in the field or accent colour, so joins belong to the film's material.
when_to_use: Mode, chapter and topic resets in textured or flat styles where a clean geometric wipe would break the material, and the hand-off into credits.
how_to_execute: Choose one motif edge for wipes per film (torn paper, page, scallop, wave).
Take the wipe colour from the current palette and fill any paper back with the outgoing field colour.
Sweep it across the frame, often diagonally, with a soft eased edge.
Let the new scene's elements slide in as the edge passes; keep small ambient elements drifting through.
Keep it fast so pacing holds.
timing: Wipe-in median about 0.5 to 0.8 s (p10 0.29 s, p90 1.5 to 2.4 s); one diagonal torn wipe 1.0 s; slower material wipes 1.4 to 3.6 s.
loom_notes: Wipe join exists; the edge shape (ragged, torn with coloured back, stitched, page curl, scallop, wave) should be a pack-level mask parameter so each pack has its own wipe.

name: Tiny subject in vast negative space
description: Scale, isolation, exposure or rarity is shown by a very small subject in a large empty field (dark or pale, often with only one strong line such as a slope or horizon) rather than by perspective or detail.
when_to_use: Introducing a thing at scale, solitude and loneliness, danger and vulnerability, rarity, the size of a problem; also making a definition unmissable.
how_to_execute: Fill the frame with one flat or gradient field; keep only faint texture or one guide line.
Shrink the subject to a few percent of the frame (well under a quarter), often low, high or off centre.
Give it the only accent or the only light.
Hold still or pull back slowly; let the subject drift slightly with the camera still.
Add a small distance or name label only if the scale is the point.
timing: Held wides of 1.8 to 14 s, most 4 to 9 s; one pull-back runs 2.6 s.
loom_notes: Composition plus wide shot sizes, pull and ambient drift. Loom's empty-frame check may flag these deliberate high-negative-space frames; record it as a gate conflict and let the layout check allow it on purpose.

name: Symmetric tableau around a central subject
description: The subject sits dead centre on a strong vertical axis flanked by mirrored figures or identical elements (guards, racks, portraits, two debaters, plants beside a monitor), or parallel elements fill symmetric parts of the frame (mirrored halves, three wedges, a hub with satellites), so the eye has one place to go.
when_to_use: Authority and formal or institutional settings, rituals, presenting a subject to be judged or defined, debates, stable factual maps, parallel events where everyone is equally affected.
how_to_execute: Centre the object of meaning, often with a nameplate or label.
Mirror identical flanking figures or props left and right; point their gazes or gestures at the centre.
For parallel events, divide the frame symmetrically and put one element in each part, staggering their changes so each lands on its own spoken beat.
Light or accent only the centre; keep motion to small flickers or one gesture.
Keep the camera static or pushing straight in; return to this wide between cutaways as the anchor.
timing: Held 1.0 to 15.2 s; wide anchor shots 3.0 to 6.4 s; one three-way staggered transform spans 11 s. Symmetric tagged in 69 shots across 9 films and 66 shots across 11 films of two batches.
loom_notes: Layout is authorable in scene code; a pedestal object would be a new object family.

name: Words and numbers written on surfaces in the world
description: Facts, dates, names and figures are lettered onto things inside the scene (a temple facade, a sign, a banner, a robe back, a train window, a phone, a whiteboard, the ground or water, a sports field) in the art's own style, rather than floated as captions.
when_to_use: Any fact, date or headline figure that can belong to an object or place; naming groups, places and topics without captions.
how_to_execute: Choose the object or surface that would naturally carry the word.
Letter it in the scene's style on that surface plane, in the accent colour for key numbers.
Write, pop, count up or reveal it (by a turn, a pan or a character passing) as it is spoken.
Keep it to one to three words or a number, and hold long enough to read.
Optionally hand the readout to the next idea (morph into a map or route).
timing: draw_on median 1.0 s; signage text median 0.05 of frame height (p10 0.03, p90 0.1); number height median 0.08 (p75 0.12); reveals by turn or pan about 1 to 2 s; holds 2 to 12 s.
loom_notes: Object states and Loom.ui artefacts carry real words, counters exist, and the iso kit places text on planes. Missing: hand-lettered numeral fonts with stroke order, sign and window surfaces as place props, and a rig back-view for text revealed by a turn.

name: A small accent traveller follows a drawn route
description: A small subject, often the only accent-coloured thing in a muted, static field, travels a drawn route: a vehicle on a dashed map line, a microbe down a tube, a book across lands, a figure between two groups or through a crowd.
when_to_use: Journeys, routes, changes of side, anomalies, the spread of an idea, a single case moving through a system.
how_to_execute: Build the static field in the base palette and draw the route first (dashed line, tube, road).
Give only the traveller the accent colour.
Move it along the route with an ease-in-out.
Pop a pin or label on arrival.
Let the camera drift with it only when the route leaves the frame; optionally end on a still close-up of the traveller.
timing: Path-follow medians 1.63 to 2.29 s (p25 1.13 s, p75 3.4 to 4.0 s, p90 6.59 s); walk-cycle medians 2.96 to 3.42 s.
loom_notes: Travel along paths exists; walk cycles are basic.

name: Near-black mode for the inner, microscopic or unknown
description: Abstract, microscopic, inner-mind or unknown beats switch the film into a near-black or navy void with one light line colour or one glowing subject and sparse drifting specks, then return to the lit world. A variant fills a character's head silhouette with the void and pins colour-blocked regions or a glowing core inside it.
when_to_use: Unknowns and open questions, inside-the-body or inside-the-system beats, mental states and cognition, a solemn verdict.
how_to_execute: Switch the field to near-black or navy (by cut, dissolve, or a morph of a head into a silhouette).
Draw with one light line colour, or one subject with a soft outer glow instead of an outline.
Add sparse drifting specks for life; use neon line-on-black for any data in this mode.
Pin labels on regions as they are named.
Return to the warm illustrated world by a dissolve or hard cut.
timing: Void beats run from 0.6 s transitions to 14.6 s explanations (inner-world shots of 2 to 15 s); void_dark backgrounds in 54 shots across 10 films of one batch and in 9 of 12 films of another.
loom_notes: Dark packs (cinematic-noir, dark-technical, glow-flat) render the look, and silhouettes, particles and labels exist. Missing: a mid-lesson mode switch to a void register inside a light pack such as editorial-paper.

name: Population grid: accent the subset, then single out one
description: A population is a uniform grid or row of identical figures or units; a share is marked by the accent (tint, cross, starburst, a wiped panel, sliced sectors), often with the number stamped across an empty band or no number at all, and the grid then collapses or zooms to one specimen to move from the many to the case.
when_to_use: Prevalence, survey results, share of a team, adoption across a population, and moving from 'many cases' to 'this one case'.
how_to_execute: Tile one simple figure or unit edge to edge on a flat field; hold briefly for 'many'.
Mark the affected share with the accent on the word, or change its faces or state marks with a stagger.
Optionally leave a horizontal empty band and stamp the number or word in it.
Recolour or scale up one unit and fade the rest, or push into one figure, or collapse the grid into a lens on one specimen.
Act on the one (label it, highlight it) and hold it as the new subject.
timing: Grid holds about 4.6 s before the collapse; grid beats 7 to 9 s; wipe in median 0.8 s, fade in median 0.54 s, scale in median 0.58 s (code); push-ins of about 6.4 s follow.
loom_notes: Unit grids, seeded arrays, recolour, scale and camera push exist. A stamped-band layout and sliced face circles would be small template parameters. Shares must come from the source.

name: Motif wave wipe that settles into a flat brand-colour end field
description: The last transition is the film's motif shape (a smooth or organic wave in the brand colour) sweeping the frame; it settles into a flat two or three colour field (brand colour, white, black) with one tiny subject and one slow action, the credits bar slides in, and the colour may later drain back to a clean field.
when_to_use: Closing a lesson with an authored, brand-consistent gesture rather than a cut to black, especially when the transition itself can be the final metaphor or when a textured film needs a decisive tonal break.
how_to_execute: Establish the band or wave shape once earlier as a motif.
Sweep it across the frame in one eased move (fast start, slow settle), swallowing the last scene.
Reduce the palette to the brand colour, white and black; draw one large flat shape (sea, landmass, grid) and one tiny dark subject.
Give the subject one small action or a slow path, and fade drifting ambient elements in step with the wipe so the field ends clean.
Slide in the fixed credits bar and hold.
Optionally drain the colour back to a clean field with a smooth ease-out under the bar.
timing: Wave or wipe shots 2.0 to 3.2 s (wipe-in median about 0.8 s, p90 2.4 s); the settled field holds about 8.5 to 20 s of credits; drain about 3 s.
loom_notes: Wipe join, flat fields and ambient motion exist; an organic or wave wipe edge taken from the pack or brand file, an accent-colour fill and a colour-drain parameter are missing. Use the client's brand colour and shape, never this channel's red device.

name: One element carries across the cut
description: A moving or held element continues across a join with matched screen position and direction (a ball's arc, a card in a hand, a cursor, a butterfly, a torch, a pose reused for a reframe, hands that slide off and become the entrance), so a change of setting reads as travel and the eye never loses the subject.
when_to_use: Moving between places or registers that share an idea while keeping one subject in view, such as a document travelling between departments, or whenever two shots should read as one gesture or one person.
how_to_execute: Choose the carrier (an object, a hand, a pose, a light, a small living element) and set it moving before the join.
Match its screen position, scale and direction on both sides of the join, or let it exit toward one edge and enter from the matching edge.
Cut on its motion, timed to the spoken keyword, or hold it in place through a dissolve while the world changes beneath it.
Let its move continue briefly into the new shot, then land it on the next keyword.
timing: The carrier's move continues about 0.3 to 1 s into the new shot; path-follow median about 1.6 to 3 s, with single carries up to about 14.5 s.
loom_notes: Travel along paths and the travel join exist inside or between stations; persisting one element's position and motion across two stations while everything else changes needs a shared-element parameter at the join.

name: Repeating pattern fills and motif bands set the place
description: Walls, water, ground, floors and backgrounds are filled with small repeating patterns or one decorative motif band (a meander border for antiquity, horizontal bands for water, a checkerboard floor as a neutral stage, a tiled wall) that imply material and era without shading, perspective or detailed backgrounds.
when_to_use: Dense storybook worlds; setting era or place in one stroke; filling negative space with texture.
how_to_execute: Choose one motif or two to three pattern tiles that signal the place.
Run them as flat bands, floors or large surface fills at low contrast so they read as texture.
Repeat the same motif across all scenes of that place.
Keep figures plain so they read against the pattern.
timing: Static and persistent; pattern backgrounds in 83 shots across 11 films of one batch.
loom_notes: Pattern fills and motif bands are not in the pack list; needs pattern tiles (meander, bands, checkerboard, tiles) as pack elements.

name: Short reset beat: dark void, flat field or calm image
description: A sub-second to roughly three-second beat with no new information resets attention: a near-black field with one glowing line, burst or word on a single spoken word, a flat colour slowly deepening, a dip to black then a bright streak, a full-frame brightness ramp, or a calm static human moment.
when_to_use: Between dense technical ideas, at a 'but', a phase change, a topic pivot, a long time jump, an open question, the end of a list, or the single biggest dramatic beat.
how_to_execute: Hard cut, or soft join (white fade, push), to the reset image.
Use a near-black or flat field with at most one shape, or a calm image with one accent and no labels.
Let only a slow tone shift, one line of light or one word move, landing on its spoken word if any.
Do not narrate new facts over it.
Leave within about a second for punctuation, a little longer for a breather.
Use a dip to black at most once per film; cluster two or three dark beats only to mark a series of open questions.
timing: Dark punctuation 0.6 to 1.2 s (FKUc8vg_Lus s016 0.6 s, NOaeKRft-gc s049 1.2 s); rest beats 0.6 to 1.4 s; brightness ramp shot 0.6 s; breathers 0.6 to 2.8 s.
loom_notes: Authorable as a short station with dip, fade, stamp or light-grow; the 'shock' join meaning fits. Conflict to resolve: Loom's empty-frame check flags these deliberate rest beats, so it needs an explicit allow marker on the beat. The narration must leave room for it.

name: Outlined foreground over ghosted, low-contrast background
description: Characters and hero props carry a uniform dark outline and full-weight line; backgrounds and secondary figures are outline-free, paler, thinner or single-hue line art in a narrow value range, so the active figure always reads first while the setting stays constant.
when_to_use: Any illustrated scene with a place behind the actor, especially a constant setting that holds a spoken list of people.
how_to_execute: Outline figures and hero props at one weight with flat fills.
Draw background shapes with no outline (or thin pale single-hue line) at reduced opacity and a narrow value range.
Swap foreground figures on each spoken item while the ghosted setting stays constant.
Fade rear crowd figures into a dense pale mass to sell depth.
Use a dark foreground element only to frame, never to compete.
timing: Static rule; foreground swaps on each spoken item.
loom_notes: Depth layers exist but packs set one outline style for all layers; needs a per-layer outline policy (figure, prop, background) with line weight and opacity so packs can ghost the back layer.

name: First scene ghosts in under the card or lifts from a white wash
description: The hand-off from the opening text card to the world is gradual: the first illustration fades up faintly behind the outgoing quote, or lifts from a white or pale wash into a hazy, low-contrast establishing view, before the first story shot.
when_to_use: Any hand-off from a text card to a scene, above all the opening card to the first image, so text eases into picture without a hard cut.
how_to_execute: Keep the outgoing card's field colour.
Start the incoming scene at very low opacity behind the text in the last part of the card, or under a near-white overlay.
Fade the text out while the scene rises to full contrast, or lift the white overlay over about 0.5 s.
Keep the establishing view low contrast and desaturated at first.
Cut to the first character or story shot once the scene has resolved.
timing: Fade-in median about 0.54 s; one establishing shot runs 0.6 s (6.0 to 6.6 s) before the first story cut; a white wash resolves over about 1 s in another film.
loom_notes: Fade and dip joins exist. The deliberate overlap of quote text and a faint scene would be flagged by Loom's double-exposure check, and a white first frame would trip the poster or empty-frame check; both are conflicts to resolve with an allowed-overlap flag for card hand-offs, not defects of the films.

name: Cross-dissolve chain of vignettes through one shared ground
description: Small self-contained vignettes on the same paper or field colour dissolve one into the next through bare ground, so very different scenes, a list or an escalation read as one surface being redrawn.
