when_to_use: Enumerating examples, steps of an escalation, a compressed historical arc, or linking a person to a place inside one hand-made world.
how_to_execute: Build each vignette as a small centred drawing on the same ground colour and texture.
Keep one warm accent on the focal item of each vignette.
Fade the outgoing drawing to bare ground and fade the next one up from it, starting on the clause boundary.
Hold each vignette long enough to read.
timing: Dissolves about 0.5 to 1 s (fade-in median 0.5 to 0.58 s, exit fade median 0.7 s); vignettes held several seconds between dissolves.
loom_notes: Fade and dissolve joins exist; build the vignettes as layers of one station so the ground never changes. Loom's double-exposure check may flag the mid-dissolve frames; the overlap is on bare ground and brief, so the check should treat it as a dissolve, not a defect.

name: Slow tilt up to a light or down to a hidden level
description: One continuous slow tilt carries the eye vertically: down from sky or canopy to ground or underground to discover a hidden level, or up from a grounded subject (onlookers, a pile of the fallen) through parallax layers to a skyline or one bright source for a hopeful or epic turn.
when_to_use: Tilt down: discovery of a hidden level, context to detail. Tilt up: hopeful or epic turns, revealing scale above a scene.
how_to_execute: Build a tall canvas with the start subject at one end and the destination at the other.
Tilt slowly in one continuous eased move through the parallax layers.
Land on the subject or the bright focal source as it is named.
timing: Tilt shots about 2.2 to 12.7 s; tilt down tagged in 15 shots across 9 films of one batch.
loom_notes: Camera move on a tall canvas, or between vertically stacked stations, exists.

name: One colour bound to one meaning for the whole film
description: Beyond the focal accent, each recurring concept, entity or side of a polarity keeps one fixed hue for the whole film (red for the threat, gold only on authority, oxygen blue and hydrogen pink, warm versus cool poles, one costume accent per recurring speaker), so the colour becomes a label and diagrams read without a legend.
when_to_use: Films that track one agent, risk or idea through many scenes and scales; topics with a small set of recurring entities (gases, roles, teams, systems); any two-way comparison or polarity held across a film.
how_to_execute: List the recurring concepts or entities and assign one hue each before any scene is drawn.
For a two-way comparison, pick one warm and one cool hue and place the pair symmetrically left and right.
Use each hue only on its concept, on every icon, particle, label, stream and character detail alike.
Never use those hues for decoration, the background or crowds, and never swap the mapping later.
Add labels only after the colours have done the separating.
timing: Film-wide; no duration.
loom_notes: Pack palette and brand tokens exist; missing is a lesson-level semantic colour map (concept to pack token) that scene builders must read and a lint that flags a mapped hue on an unmapped element.

name: People, crowds and threats as flat silhouettes
description: Crowds, operators, authorities and threats are flat featureless silhouettes (near-black or one flat colour), sometimes with a thin glowing rim on dark fields, looping two or three gestures; the one figure that matters is drawn in full colour or given the only accent, white fill or rim. Pose, not face, carries emotion.
when_to_use: Collectives, public reaction, users, teams, unknown authorities, menace, serious segments and any crowd that would cost detail; isolating one actor from many.
how_to_execute: Fill the figures solid near-black or one flat field colour with no interior detail.
Place them on a soft radial or vertical gradient, or add a thin pale rim stroke, for edge contrast.
Stagger a two or three pose loop across a crowd; keep it near static.
Draw only the subject in full colour, or give it the only accent, white fill or rim colour.
Show operators from behind so the screen they face is the subject.
Resolve a silhouette into a coloured named figure on the spoken name if it becomes a person.
Cut from the wide mass to a tight isolated figure to dramatise many to one.
timing: Silhouette impact beats 0.8 to 2.4 s; silhouette processions and group drifts hold 5 to 10 s (walk cycles median 1.75 s, code).
loom_notes: Fills are pack-driven and seeded arrays and staggered groups exist, so a crowd can be built. Missing: a silhouette shading mode on rigs (solid fill plus optional rim stroke and accent eyes) and an isolate-one parameter. Glowing eyes and monster silhouettes read as menace; for employees prefer plain silhouettes with one accent.

name: The subject object gets a minimal face
description: An inanimate thing or component (a folder, a cell, an organ, a material, a device, a metronome) keeps its real silhouette and gains two dot eyes and one curve, sometimes thin stick arms, so it can carry strain or relief; its expression changes with its state and it may act out each property with one prop.
when_to_use: Making a tool, a file, a component or a material approachable; showing strain or relief inside a system; explaining properties of a thing with no natural actor.
how_to_execute: Keep the object's real silhouette and add two dot eyes and one curve, nothing more.
Map states to three expressions: neutral, strained, relieved.
Change the expression on the word that names the effect.
Optionally give it thin arms (never legs) and hand it one prop per property.
Keep the face small so the diagram still reads as a diagram.
Keep the same design for the whole film.
timing: character_act median 0.5 to 0.63 s (code); a whole property demonstration runs within a 10.6 s shot; single emotional beats 2.4 to 3.4 s.
loom_notes: Object families have states but no face layer; a small face kit (eyes, brows, mouth curves) attachable to any object grammar would cover most uses. Arms and props make it an object-mascot rig, which is a new primitive. Use with restraint for corporate learners: a face on a document or a tool reads friendly; a cute mascot on a serious compliance point can read childish.

name: Map as a still stage, one marker per named place
description: A flat or desaturated map is held still as a stage while one small uniform icon, warm object or marker pops onto each place as it is named, staggered in the direction of spread, with a dated label stamped over it and dashed routes drawn for movement.
when_to_use: Where and when something began, spread, was adopted or banned; rollouts; a global footprint.
how_to_execute: Hard cut to a static two-tone or desaturated map; keep the camera locked, or pan slowly if wider than the frame.
Pop one uniform marker per named place on its word, all in one warm accent.
Stagger in the direction of spread.
Stamp a dated label when the year matters.
Draw dashed routes in travel order for movement.
timing: pop_in median 0.46 to 0.58 s per marker (code); map builds run 4 to 10 s.
loom_notes: Real geography (world map, globe), pops and dashed paths exist; a hand-drawn map finish is a pack matter. Places and dates must come from the source.

name: The number lives on an object in the scene
description: A spoken number is an oversized object or part of one, not a caption: a price tag, a sign, a check, a hand-lettered bag, a meter bar or a glowing counter over the field it measures. Counters tick through intermediate values while a container fills or an object scales in steps with the figure.
when_to_use: Headline totals, prices, rates, codes and any statistic the learner should remember.
how_to_execute: Put the number on or in an object from the story (sign, bag, counter, container, body).
Set it at least twice the label height (number height median 0.08 to 0.12 of frame height against labels near 0.05).
Pop or type it on with the spoken value; use the accent only on the digits.
For a change, tick a counter through intermediate values while a container fills or the object scales in discrete steps.
Let the object enact the number right after (break, split, overflow).
Morph the number in place when it grows.
timing: pop_in median 0.46 s; number morphs in place over about 1 s; counter climbs about 8 s; scale steps median 0.58 s; container cycles over 15.8 to 19.4 s shots.
loom_notes: Counters, objects and glow exist. A binding from a counter value to an object's scale or fill level, and hand-lettered number labels on props, are small parameters. Every number must trace to the source.

name: Call-to-action end card with a link or code
description: A clean centred end card holds a URL in heavy sans or a scannable code with a pill-shaped link, over a pale field or a calm illustrated backdrop with a few slowly drifting shapes, while the credits bar runs.
when_to_use: When the lesson hands the viewer to a next step: a course, a form, a resource.
how_to_execute: Clear the frame to a pale field or a quiet image.
Centre the link or code and one pill button; keep the one accent colour only on the actionable element.
Pop or scale the link in with a soft ease-out as the narration says it.
Drift two or three soft shapes in the margins.
Slide the credits bar up and hold the card still for the spoken offer.
timing: End cards of about 10 to 12 s; credits 6.5 to 18.7 s.
loom_notes: Title and recap templates cover it; a QR code generator is a small addition. For employees the target is an LMS link or next action, not a sponsor.

name: An object grows into the frame or layout of the next shot
description: A symbol or carried object from one shot is kept in place and reused as the structure of the next: an emblem ring becomes a tunnel mask, a machine flattens into a face-on dial, a folder opens into a grid of people, a flag's colour bands become map zones, door posts become wire posts.
when_to_use: Shifting from what something looks like to how it works, from a symbol to its subject, or when the next idea literally grows out of the last (unification, publication, a scale jump).
how_to_execute: Identify a shape both scenes can share (bands, verticals, a ring, a rectangle).
End the outgoing shot on that strong central shape and grow it toward full frame.
Keep it in place while changing what it is: a mask, a face-on dial, a container.
Map its geometry onto the incoming layout and let the new content grow out of or through it.
Complete the transform on the spoken title or naming word.
timing: Transform-into median 1.0 to 1.3 s (p75 2.1 s); single cases run 1.4 to 5.4 s.
loom_notes: The continue join holds the picture and changes it; using an outgoing shape as a mask portal into the next station, and shape matching between outgoing and incoming layouts, are parameters (plus the morph gap of outline_morph_join).

name: A bright line or dot stream traces a flow through a system
description: An invisible flow becomes a path the eye can follow: one high-contrast line or marker travels from input to target, lighting each component or node as it passes and blooming at the target, or a stream of small accent dots moves along thin channels and bunches where they narrow.
when_to_use: Signals, light paths, energy, data, air or blood moving through a machine, network or body; throughput and bottlenecks.
how_to_execute: Draw the structure or channel network first, thin and muted (or as a wireframe or cutaway on a dark field).
Draw on one accent line from the source, or spawn small accent dots there.
Move along the paths at a steady rate.
Recolour or light each component as the marker reaches it; slow and bunch dots where a channel narrows.
Bloom the target on its spoken name, optionally with a slow push-in, or pan along a long object.
timing: Path-follow medians 1.63 to 3.04 s (p75 4.2 s, p90 7.84 s); draw-on medians 0.67 to 1.08 s; particle bursts median 1.4 s (p90 5.0 s); shots of 3.4 to 4.2 s (2A1IEBFt6Xg s015, s024).
loom_notes: Draw-on, travel along paths, particles and glow (glow-flat) exist.

name: Persistent border or shaped vignette around the scene
description: A container shape frames the scene for the whole film or for one kind of content: a torn-paper or hand-drawn border, an ornamental or doodle border, a centred circle or porthole, an oval, rounded or ragged ink-blot vignette. Scenes change inside it while it stays fixed, so cuts read as turning pages, and a shape can mark tale, memory or lens space against full-frame present-day diagrams.
when_to_use: Archival, history and storybook films with many vignettes; technical films that want warmth at the edges and clean diagrams inside; separating memory, tale or diagram space from the main world; instrument, lens or microscopic scale jumps; a brand container.
how_to_execute: Choose one container per meaning and keep it for the whole film (border for identity; circle for lens; oval or ink blot for memory or tale).
Place every relevant scene inside it on a flat contrasting field, with diagram content inside a clear margin.
Keep the container fixed while scenes slide, wipe or dissolve inside it; never break it.
Run present-day content full frame so the contrast reads.
Open a circular container by fading it up from low contrast; keep the next subject centred in the same circle across the join.
Let small border items drift at low opacity for ambient life; optionally push the camera through the vignette to change scene.
timing: Persistent; one circle opening fades up over about 0.5 s; inner dissolves inside 10.3 s plates.
loom_notes: A frame layer, the iris join and the vignette shader exist; missing are container mask shapes as pack options (circle, rounded rect, oval, ragged ink, torn edge) and the ornamental, doodle and torn-paper border artwork as assets.

name: A recurring presenter or figure at a fixed home station
description: One figure (an expert at a desk, a host, two advocates at lecterns, a person in a symmetric corridor or armchair) returns at the same fixed, often symmetric location between diagram or evidence inserts, speaking with lip sync or holding with a faint idle sway, so a long or multi-world lesson has a narrative home.
when_to_use: Long technical lessons, multi-world explanations and anything that needs an anchor and a takeaway voice between mechanism segments.
how_to_execute: Design one figure and one fixed, symmetric set.
Frame close or medium, static, with constant framing and accent.
Drive the mouth from word timings; add brow and small head tilts at sentence turns.
Cut back to the station after every two or three inserts.
Give it one gesture per return, on the takeaway word.
Use a slow push-in on the station for emphasis.
timing: Returns of 4.8 to 8.4 s; lip_sync segments median 1.04 s (p75 4.2 s; code); one film returns to the same corridor about ten times.
loom_notes: Presenter template, rigs and lip sync from word timings exist. A 'home station' role in the storyboard would make the return rhythm explicit and checkable.

name: One shape grows over a held frame
description: Everything holds while one high-contrast shape grows or fills in two or three discrete stages inside a fixed structure (a cavity, a crystal, a liquid level, a blockage, a progress bar), so accumulation is watched rather than told and stops on the spoken end state.
when_to_use: Slow processes, build-ups, blockages, backlogs, depletion, load in a system, progress.
how_to_execute: Draw the structure once and hold it; remove the presenter if needed.
Make the growing shape the only high-contrast element.
Grow it with a slow ease, or in two or three stages each tied to a spoken phrase.
Add fine detail by draw-on at its word.
Stop on the spoken end state.
timing: grow median 1.38 to 1.5 s (p75 2.5 to 3.0 s, p90 4.96 s; code); one cavity grows across a 17.0 s held shot; staged fills in 5.4 to 11.2 s shots.
loom_notes: Grow, reveal and charts that build exist; a staged fill along a path inside a shape would be a convenience parameter.

name: Hold intact, then break on the word
description: An object, figure or word is held intact for a beat, then cracks, shatters, crumples or is struck in one fast burst on the key word, a few shards or one red mark follow, and the result holds still so the change has weight; crumpling also removes old elements to clear the frame.
when_to_use: Failures, collapse, a rule being broken, obsolescence, rupture, sudden shock, violence shown without detail.
how_to_execute: Show the object whole and still in its material; hold about two seconds.
Break it on the word with a held-then-fast ease-out burst.
Use shards of the same fill, a small particle burst, or a single red mark; never more.
Hold the rubble or result still for the next line.
Clear fragments before the next idea, or use the removal itself to clear the frame for a replacement.
timing: Intact hold about 2.0 s (QyRqlTV60zM s040), then the break over a sub-second to 1.8 s (s041); ease-out move median 0.96 s; exit scale median 0.5 s; impact shot 1.4 s (mzREA81VQ34 s060).
loom_notes: Stamp, pop, particles and ease-out exist, but there is no crumple, crack or shatter primitive; a few-large-shards builder would cover most uses.

name: Diagram assembled part by part as the parts are named
description: A mechanism or system diagram is built on one held frame in the order the narration names its parts, starting from the bare central object, so the viewer builds the machine in step with the voice; connecting lines are drawn only after both of their ends exist.
when_to_use: Mechanisms, procedures and system diagrams.
how_to_execute: Write the narration so parts are named in assembly order.
Start from the bare central object on a held frame.
Bring each part in on its word with a pop, slide or draw-on.
Draw connecting lines only after both ends exist.
Hold the finished assembly before the next idea.
timing: Builds run about 10 to 16 s on one held frame (QyRqlTV60zM s073 14.8 s, ul-c6a4QkiU s020b 15.9 s); pop-in median 0.5 s, draw-on median 0.67 s per part.
loom_notes: Word timings drive cues. Missing: a gate that fails any part appearing before its word and any connector drawn before both ends exist (seen in QyRqlTV60zM s070 and P5pmMe3EarI s041).

name: Whole-frame palette shift while the composition holds
description: The layout and subject hold still while the colour of the whole frame changes: the field washes to a new hue, the palette flips (dark cool to bright green), the colour temperature ramps to an alarm hue, or the scene saturates up from washed-out. The change itself is the event, with no cut.
when_to_use: A new beat about the same subject, relief after pressure, an alarm, danger or failure introduced without cutting away, an arrival or memory surfacing, demonstrating an improvement.
how_to_execute: Hold the subject and layout in place; keep the subject's pose still so the change reads as environmental.
On the keyword, cross-fade the field hue, flip the whole palette, or ramp the temperature (blue to pink, normal to red).
For an arrival, start at low saturation and high brightness and animate saturation and contrast up.
For an emotional turn, change the palette and the pose together.
Follow an alarm with the measurable consequence (a gauge drains, a glow turns red).
timing: colour_change median 0.8 s (p75 1.4 s); light change median 0.79 s (p75 2.6 s); saturation ramps 0.5 to 1.4 s; one alert shot runs 7.2 s.
loom_notes: The continue join (hold the picture and change it), colour tweens, the shader light layer and the heat hold-and-transform cover it.

name: Inner state as a symbol, prop or glowing marks on the figure
description: A feeling or mental state becomes one visible thing over or inside an otherwise still, reduced figure: a watching eye, a lit chest, a scribble knot, a rain cloud, a flame, an orb, or a few small glowing marks on a dark silhouette; it grows in stages, wobbles slowly and resolves when the state changes.
when_to_use: Emotions, pressure, uncertainty, motivation, focus and invisible cognitive states in people-centred lessons.
how_to_execute: Hold the figure still, reduced and in a matching posture.
Fade or pop the symbol above the head or on the chest on the named state; grow it in stages timed to words.
Give it the accent and a soft glow, with a slow organic wobble or orbit.
For a dark silhouette on a saturated field, pop small bright marks one by one.
Resolve it (fade, warm, transform) when the intervention is named; optionally pull back to share the feeling.
timing: Symbol builds over 2 to 5 s; marks pop at pop_in median 0.5 s; ambient wobble median 5.2 s (code); a glow can hold 9.8 s.
loom_notes: Glow, particles and draw-on exist, so it is composable today; a head or chest anchored prop socket on rigs is the parameter that would make it reliable.

name: Personify the invisible actor and keep it for every step
description: The invisible or abstract actor (a virus, a signal, a policy, a brain function, a molecule) becomes one small character, or a small set of agent types, with a fixed silhouette, colour and face grammar; it physically performs each step (carries, reads, ticks, squeezes, blocks, operates) and recurs across scenes so each diagram feels like a continuation.
when_to_use: Multi-step processes whose actor is invisible; it gives the learner one thing to follow.
how_to_execute: Design one or two agent types with a fixed simple silhouette, one colour and a fixed face grammar.
Introduce it singled out from many, or sliding in as it is named, with a written label once.
Let it act each step physically on the subject: carry, read, tick, squeeze, block, operate.
Use expression changes, not new characters, for state changes.
Let bystanders react so the cause is read from their faces.
Carry the same agent across joins.
timing: Character acts median 0.5 s, p90 2.0 s (code); an agent appears across 5 to 7 cited shots per film; introductions about 2 s.
loom_notes: Rigs support poses, gestures and blinks but are people; there is no blob or object-with-face character family. Needs a small rigged agent set per lesson (or per pack). For corporate audiences a neutral geometric agent (a token, a packet) reads better than a cute creature.

name: One facial feature changes on the cue
description: A state change is carried by one feature on an otherwise static face: a mouth curve flips, an eye snaps open or narrows, X-eyes or a badge text swap instantly; for escalating feelings, a held close-up steps through two or three discrete expressions of rising intensity with the peak on the key word and one punctuation mark (sweat drop, tear, small starburst).
when_to_use: Reaction beats (startle, doubt, dread, realisation), the emotional cost of a fact, and sensitive or formal outcomes that should read clearly but not graphically.
how_to_execute: Hold the body and the rest of the face still; a symmetric close-up works for eyes-only beats.
Change only one feature on the spoken cue, as an instant swap or a morph under 1 s.
For escalation, define two or three expression poses and step between them on phrase boundaries, peak on the key word.
Add one secondary cue at the peak only (sweat drop, tear, starburst).
Hold a beat on the new state.
timing: Feature changes instant to under 1 s; character_act median 0.92 s in one batch (code); stepped close-ups of 3.6 to 4.2 s with three stages; an eyes-only beat sits in a 1.8 s shot.
loom_notes: Rig expressions, blinks and text swaps exist. Missing: an expression sequence keyed to word timings with a peak-word marker, and an eye-shape morph parameter on the face rig.

name: Drop into a situation already in progress
description: Straight after the card the film drops into peril, a mystery or a trial already under way (a ship in a storm, a skier caught, a hearing in session, a calm float broken by an alarm), so a question is posed before any explanation and the answer is held back.
when_to_use: Hooks for safety, risk, mechanism and history lessons that can be framed as a problem in progress.
how_to_execute: Open on a calm or tense baseline already in motion for one or two shots.
Introduce the disturbance in a few fast cuts within the first 10 to 20 s.
End the run on a single image that poses the question.
Hold the answer back until the definition section, then begin the explanation.
timing: Seconds to the first question 8 to about 25 s in these films (records).
loom_notes: Storyboard decision; story-cartoon places, characters and charts that build (for an alarm gauge) exist. Keep peril professional for employee audiences.

name: Section card as a quiet reset
description: A short title card marks each section or numbered step with little motion: a tilted paper strip, hand-lettered slab, torn question card or patterned curtain, or letters made of the film's own material (clay, cut paper, marker) with a step-number badge.
when_to_use: Between modules, before a turn from story to mechanism, and in multi-step or numbered lessons so the sequence is felt.
how_to_execute: Design one card format per film and reuse it for every section.
Put one short phrase on it, built in the world's material, slightly tilted with a soft shadow.
Add a step number as a corner badge or ribbon when the lesson is numbered.
Give it at most a small swell or wobble, or ease the tilt upright, or type the phrase word by word.
Hold still so it can be read, then cut or wipe straight into the first image of the section.
timing: Cards hold 0.6 to 3.2 s (gVXoAbeB8QI s030 2.0 s, YtCpZnBhWZ0 s105 0.6 s); one title builds in a single 1.2 s ease-in-out.
loom_notes: The title template exists; tilt, paper-strip backplate, brush script, pack material variants and a step-badge slot are parameters. Clay letters need assets.

name: One shape morphs through a chain of meanings in place
description: A single centred object transforms in the same spot through several stages or symbols (dots to a question mark to a word; a flask to a molecule; raw input to finished output), each stage landing on one spoken beat, and the answer is revealed only at the last stage, so the eye never travels.
when_to_use: A concept that escalates or changes meaning; processes from raw input to finished output; build-ups with a payoff.
how_to_execute: Centre one object on an empty field.
Design every stage on a shared silhouette, in narration order, each tied to its keyword.
Morph each stage into the next in place, keeping size and position.
Keep one small accent constant across stages as an anchor binding cause and effect.
Reveal the final identity last, optionally with an emphasis shape behind it; hold it, or scale it to the frame edge as the exit.
timing: Morph medians 1.0 to 1.17 s per stage (p25 0.63 s, p75 1.71 s); some morphs run under 1 s; one four-stage chain spans 7.8 s.
loom_notes: Hold-and-transform (lift, heat, peel) exists, but there is no path interpolation between arbitrary shapes and no sequence parameter for chained stages with designed intermediates.

name: Callout badge that names a person on the spoken name
description: Each speaker or person mentioned is introduced by one recurring callout shape (a hand-drawn starburst, spiky badge, hexagon card with a pointer tail, or a flat saturated nameplate) carrying name and role, often the only saturated element in a muted shot; it pops in as the name is spoken, sits clear of the face, and exits before the person's content.
when_to_use: Multi-speaker lessons where lower thirds would feel corporate and linger; flagging the named item in a busy collage; introducing historical figures without photos.
how_to_execute: Choose one callout shape family for the film.
Letter one to three words (name and role) inside it in marker or the film's hand.
Place it in a lower corner or near a shoulder, clear of the face.
Pop it in with a springy scale as the name is spoken, or type the name on a flat plate letter by letter.
Exit it (shrink out or fade) after about 2 s, before the first content sticker enters.
timing: pop_in median 0.5 s; badges held about 2 s or for the length of the name; observed by the vision model as landing on the name (not a measured offset); badge text 0.05 to 0.12 of frame.
loom_notes: Pop, stamp and typewriter exist; needs a badge or label template with callout plates (starburst, hexagon with tail, nameplate) and enter and exit tied to the name word. Line-art portraits need rig or asset work.

name: The opening set returns, changed, at the close
description: The opening tableau, landscape or illustrated set returns at the end, changed in one way (emptied, desaturated, a falling leaf, a montage of clips on its screen), so the film ends where it began and a series reads as one show.
when_to_use: Story-led lessons, series and client programmes where closure and one identity matter.
how_to_execute: Plan the closing frame when designing the opening.
Reuse the same composition and palette (for a series, keep the set palette constant).
Optionally open by powering a central screen on and diving through it.
Change one thing at the close to carry the lesson.
Lay credits over the returning set.
timing: Opening set holds 1.6 to 3.2 s before a dive; closing tableau 10 to 18.2 s.
loom_notes: Stations can be reused; the storyboard should name the bookend explicitly. A studio set with a live screen showing footage needs assets and compositing.

name: One figure multiplies into a row or crowd of near-identical variants
description: A population is a row, grid or field of one figure repeated with three to five small variations (hair, coat colour, pose), often made by multiplying one representative figure on the word that names the group; the camera pans or drifts along the row so more is implied than shown.
when_to_use: Workforce size, how common a habit or condition is, one versus many, organisations at work.
how_to_execute: Show one figure doing the representative action.
On the word that names the group, multiply it into a row or grid with even spacing.
Vary only one small attribute per copy; keep them in the field colour.
Recolour only the one that matters, if any.
After a short settle, drift or pan the camera along the row, or pull out to reveal the extent.
timing: Pans and pull-outs to reveal a crowd take 2 to 10 s; one cited figure-to-drifting-row runs 9.0 s across three shots.
loom_notes: Seeded arrays, staggered groups and camera pans exist. The one-into-many multiplication would use the same hold-and-transform gap as other morphs; a cross-fade or stagger-in is the available substitute.

name: Thought or speech bubble with a nested, changing picture
description: A bubble above a held figure holds a sequence of small vignettes that cross-fade per clause (a wish, a calculation, a memory, a named term), drawn smaller and lighter than reality; the content can pop out into the world or fade as the real thing fades in. Speech can be shown the same way as icon glyphs popping one per key word into rounded bubbles, without written words.
when_to_use: Plans, calculations, memories, beliefs, imagined outcomes and decisions; conversations whose content matters less than the fact of the exchange, or that must read without subtitles.
how_to_execute: Pose the thinker or speakers once and hold; place two speakers symmetrically.
Pop the bubble (cloud with a dotted tail for thought, rounded for speech) on the spoken cue.
Draw the content smaller and lighter than reality, or one hand-lettered word.
Cross-fade each new content on its clause, or pop one glyph per key word into a speech bubble.
Let the thinker's eyes track it; keep bodies near static.
Resolve: pop the object out into the world, fade the bubble as the real object fades in, or fade bubbles out in order.
timing: Bubble and glyph pops about 0.4 to 0.46 s (pop_in median, code); contents cross-fade per clause; one glyph exchange spans about 17 s.
loom_notes: Pops, fades and chat UI with real words exist. Missing: a bubble component per pack with a nested scene slot that cross-fades its children, and a glyph-only sequence driven by word timings. Conflict to resolve: Loom's double-exposure check may flag the per-clause cross-fades inside the bubble, which these films do on purpose.

name: Ghost or glowing double of a figure for the non-physical
description: A semi-transparent duplicate or a soft glowing silhouette is laid over or beside a real figure drawn crisply: the self that wants to act, an inner voice or ideal, an intruding association, or white silhouettes reconstructing an unseen event over static evidence. It changes shape in place for each emotional turn.
when_to_use: Wanting versus being able, assumptions and mental models, retrieval errors, reconstructing what happened, or implying people who are normally there.
how_to_execute: Hold the base scene static and keep real people in the pack's crisp outlined style.
Fade in a low-opacity duplicate, a featureless white silhouette, or a blurred-edge glow in one reserved cool colour.
Show one moment per silhouette and fade it before the next.
Use dashed outlines for things the ghost imagines.
Keep the evidence or the real figure the brightest element; morph the ghost slowly in place for its changes.
timing: fade_in median 0.5 s, exit_fade median 0.54 s (code); one silhouette per narrated moment; a ghost-to-reflection morph takes about 3 s.
loom_notes: An opacity copy of a rig or a silhouette fill is possible with current layers, and glow exists in glow-flat and the shader layer. Needs a glow figure style usable inside other packs. Conflict to resolve: Loom's double-exposure check would flag these deliberate ghost holds.

name: A spoken list, one item per beat, in one place
description: A spoken list is enumerated without the eye wandering: each item lights its location on a held diagram or illustration with a leader line and a colour-matched label, or swaps the glyph inside one fixed central container, or pops as one icon of a single family in a row with a one-word label.
when_to_use: Lists of components, affected systems, touchpoints, factors, risks, qualities, takeaways or roles.
how_to_execute: Choose the holder: the diagram the items live on, one central container, or a row.
On each spoken item, light its region or scale in a highlight circle, swap the inner glyph, or pop the next icon left to right.
Add a short label by leader line or a matching bullet; headline type heavy, list type light.
Keep the accent on the current item only.
For long rows, truck the camera at a slow constant speed.
Close with a highlight on the key item, then slide the set out together.
timing: pop_in median 0.5 s per item, scale_in median 0.92 s (code); whole lists in 6.4 to 8.2 s; carousel shots 11 to 19 s; one row truck about 19 s.
loom_notes: List, icon-grid templates, labels, draw-on and staggered pops exist, with the one-icon-family rule. Region highlighting needs the diagram built with named parts; a single-slot carousel driven by word timings is a template variant.

name: Before and after on identical geometry
description: Two states or versions of one place or object (old and new design, wood and stone, before and after an improvement) cross-dissolve, wipe or swap in exactly the same position and geometry while callouts stay fixed, so only the changed parts move and the change reads as time.
when_to_use: Upgrades, before and after, material or tool changes, time jumps and re-interpretations where the constant matters as much as the change.
how_to_execute: Draw the after state on exactly the same geometry as the before state; lock any numbered callouts.
Keep the shared structure grey or muted in both states.
Add the accent colour or new props only in the after state.
Optionally push in slowly on the focal object.
Cross-dissolve, wipe or swap on the comparison word; swap only a small time label to mark an era.
Hold the after state for the rest of the beat.
timing: Wipe-in median about 1.0 s; swaps observed on the spoken comparison word; shots of 4.4 to 14.8 s.
loom_notes: The continue join (hold the picture and change it) plus an accent-layer fade covers it; the scene builder must keep shared geometry between the two states.

name: Circular iris or lens window opens onto the next scene
description: A circle grows from the centre or from a subject until it fills the frame with the next scene inside it, or closes onto a symbol to end a beat; with a dark rim it reads as a lens into a detail or cross-section, and after a black shape swallows the frame it reads as rebirth into an enclosed space.
when_to_use: Scale shifts from whole to detail, moving from a scene to the single cause inside it, closing an idea on a symbol, and dark or descending registers.
how_to_execute: Place a small circular window over the subject of interest, or at the centre.
Pick the circle colour or rim from the incoming field; add a dark rim if it should read as a lens.
Grow it over the last moment of the shot until it fills the frame, revealing the next scene inside it (or close it onto a symbol).
For the void variant, spread an organic black shape from inside the picture, hold black very briefly, then open the iris with the subject low in frame.
Land the full-frame state on the word that names the detail.
timing: Scale-in median about 0.67 s; iris shots of about 3.4 s; the void-and-iris pair spans much longer shots (7.8 s and 16 s) in one film.
loom_notes: The iris join exists; a lens rim is a styling parameter and an organic spreading black shape is a wipe-edge parameter.

name: Dip through white for a soft stop, through black for a time jump
description: A held beat dips to a white or pale wash and the next scene fades up from it, a gentle stop between ideas; a dip through black marks a time jump, a shift between a frame story and the tale inside it, or finality. Neither is used for ordinary idea changes.
when_to_use: White: ending an emotional or mechanism beat before a topic change. Black: time skips, story-within-story shifts, solemn endings.
how_to_execute: Hold the outgoing picture still, on a low-motion frame.
Raise a white or pale overlay, or fade to black, over a fraction of a second.
Fade the next scene up from the same wash; from black, let the light come up on a dim scene.
Keep one accent alive through a white fade if a reference point is needed.
timing: Fade-ups from white about 0.25 to 0.5 s; exit fade median about 0.58 s; light change median about 1.0 s.
loom_notes: The dip join exists with white or black and the time meaning; the white first frame and the black hold may trip the empty-frame check, which should accept a dip that is a deliberate rest beat.

name: A foreground object exits to reveal the next subject
description: The largest object in frame, or a foreground occluder (a body, a panel, a door, a trunk, a pair of hands), slides off in the direction of its motion and its exit uncovers the subject already in place behind it, on the spoken name.
when_to_use: Introducing the person or thing a segment is about, cause-and-effect beats where the moving object is the cause, experiments where hidden position matters, calm hand-offs on one continuous ground.
how_to_execute: Place the occluder in the foreground layer covering the subject, as the largest element in frame.
Hold the camera static and keep the background identical across the change.
Slide the occluder off on the spoken name, in the direction of its motion.
Let the revealed subject blink or turn once for life.
timing: Exit-slide median about 0.8 s; slide-in median about 0.67 s.
loom_notes: Unmask, depth layers, and travel or continue joins with 'outgoing elements leave first' cover it.

name: One accent burst or flash on the impact word
description: A single flat spiky starburst, radial burst or full-frame accent flash pops at the contact point or behind the subject exactly on the word of a handoff, reveal or impact, then goes; never several at once.
when_to_use: Payoffs, receipts, reveals, a term being named, impacts and sudden emotion: a beat that must punch.
how_to_execute: Hold the action until the key word.
Pop one burst in the accent colour behind the subject or at the contact point, or flash the whole frame one accent colour.
Keep it under a quarter of the shot.
Remove it quickly and return to the muted field.
timing: Pop-in median 0.4 s; flash shots run 0.6 to 1.2 s (56F0Y33QZnQ s019 0.6 s, s022 1.2 s).
loom_notes: Pop, stamp and synthesised hit effects exist; a starburst shape family and a one-frame flash or inversion are not in the object or join lists.

name: One subject steps through its states in place
description: A process on one figure or object is shown where it stands: it decays, swells, heals, matures or changes colour and texture in steps, one per spoken stage, with a label per state, while outline, position and set stay fixed.
when_to_use: Processes over time, lifecycles of one thing (healing, wearing, loading, maturing) and before and after states where the environment must stay constant.
how_to_execute: Centre one clean subject in a static set or on a flat field.
Keep its outline and position fixed; mark the affected region with a small accent band or texture patch if the change is local.
Step through the states, each landing on its spoken stage word.
Pop a label per state and fade it before the next.
Hold the end state.
timing: Morph median 1.5 s (p25 0.5 s, p75 2.21 s); colour change median 1.13 s; a full sequence runs about 4 to 15 s (ul-c6a4QkiU s007b 14.8 s).
loom_notes: Colour and texture steps are possible with hold-and-transform states; smooth shape changes between states (a face decaying, an organ ballooning) need a path-morph primitive.

name: Arrival burst, then a reading hold
description: Inside one shot all elements arrive in a short burst at the cut or reveal, then the frame holds nearly still for the back half while the voice explains.
when_to_use: Diagrams and data that must be read.
how_to_execute: Put all arrivals in the first part of the shot.
Hold the finished diagram static for the back half.
Keep only an ambient loop during the hold.
Cut or transform only after the sentence lands.
timing: Records describe back-half holds in 13 to 15 s shots (UQdtUaeZWLo s007a, s012a). Corpus longest still stretch per film (code): median 5 s, maximum 24 s.
loom_notes: Motion timing is per scene. Missing: a check that the last third of a diagram beat is calm.

name: State change as a colour swap on a held object or layout
description: The layout never redraws; the current step or state is shown by changing the fill of the object itself: an active button turns green, pipes flood red, a ring of a plan turns red, an object desaturates and sinks to go dormant or saturates and rises to wake, a status light turns green to red before the event.
when_to_use: Machines, pipelines and step-by-step processes; stepping through nested layers; dormant versus active, safe versus failing, before versus after.
how_to_execute: Draw the layout once and hold it.
Assign one colour meaning per state.
On the spoken step, tween the fill toward the new state colour.
Pair the colour change with one physical cue (sink, rise, crack) where it helps.
Change colour first, then shape, so cause reads before effect.
Step a highlight through nested parts in order.
timing: colour_change median 0.6 to 1.0 s (p25 0.5, p75 1.0 to 2.0).
loom_notes: Colour change on a held station, colour tweens and the heat hold-and-transform cover it.

name: Crowd of repeated glyphs with one active member
description: Crowds and populations are a dense texture of one repeated simple face or silhouette with tiny variations, held still or given only a slow camera drift, and only the one or two focal members move or carry the accent.
when_to_use: Large groups, audiences, workforces, conforming masses; showing a category while pointing at one member.
how_to_execute: Repeat one figure across the area in a grid, row or mass with tiny variations (hood, tilt).
Keep the mass in the base palette and still (eyes closed, no sway), or add only a slow drift or faint shimmer.
Animate only the focal member with small timed gestures.
Reserve the accent for the one individual who matters.
timing: Drifts up to 9.8 s; character beats median 0.92 s; one 11 s shot carries four timed beats on the focal member.
loom_notes: Seeded arrays, unit grids and staggered groups exist.

name: Readable text written on word by word with the voice
description: When words must be read (a question, a key sentence, a lyric, a decree, a quoted source, a date), they type or write on word by word in sync with the narration, often on a physical artefact inside the world (scroll, sticky note, held note, chalkboard), never as a flat slide.
when_to_use: Questions, key sentences, quoting policy, a source, a definition or an example the learner must read.
how_to_execute: Set the line or choose an artefact that fits the world (note, scroll, board, document).
Slide or pin the artefact in with a small overshoot and settle; tilt it slightly.
Reveal one word per spoken word; highlight the key word in the accent.
Hold the finished text still long enough to be read.
For abstract agreements, draw thin rules as body text and pop only the real title.
timing: Matches speech rate (median 138.9 wpm in one batch); written notes held 9.2 to 13.8 s.
loom_notes: Typewriter with word timings, draw-on and document artefacts with real words exist; paper-note and chalkboard skins are pack assets.

name: One held object, one attribute or symbol swapped
description: A long timeline or a state change is compressed into one held object whose single attribute or symbol swaps per spoken era or turn: a flag's colours per owner, hair drifting to grey, a window cycling day and night, a battery icon gaining a red X, a closed sign hung on a structure.
when_to_use: Chains of owners, versions or phases; passage of time around a fixed subject; failures, stopping and rules.
how_to_execute: Establish the object with a quick scale-in, then hold it and the camera static.
Pick one attribute to change (colour, hair, light) or one universal symbol.
Swap it on each named era or on the narrative turn, as a hard cut or a morph of about 1 s.
Keep the rest of the frame on a flat two-band field; let a small expression change confirm a failure.
timing: colour_change median 1.0 s (code); one flag-swap shot runs 18.2 s; in-shot swaps are a hard cut or about 1 s.
loom_notes: Colour tweens on word timings and object states (phone, document, lock) cover it; sign objects would need adding.

name: Camera travel between stations instead of a cut
description: Instead of cutting, the camera trucks or pans across one wide board, desk, map or panel grid from one explanation station to the next, with one element (a flagged node, a path) persisting across the seam, so position and connection are part of the explanation.
when_to_use: Tours of a system (a facility, a desk of notes, a scroll of vignettes), or linking an abstract diagram to the concrete place it affects.
how_to_execute: Lay all stations side by side on one wide canvas.
Keep one element across the seam between stations.
Hold on a station while it is explained.
Travel with an eased start and stop to the next station; the outgoing content leaves as the incoming enters.
Settle on the new subject before the next spoken beat.
timing: Travels of about 2.8 to 18 s; they are rare, since the camera is static in most shots.
loom_notes: The camera move between stations exists.

name: Close on a spoken open question over a symbolic image
description: The last narrated beat poses an open question or a quiet invitation in voice, not on screen, carried by one simple symbolic image (a boat on a wave, a lone figure, a ring of dots) with slow continuous motion, then rolls into the credits.
when_to_use: Ending lessons that should prompt reflection or a next step rather than a summary.
how_to_execute: Return to one simple symbolic image.
State the question in the narration, not as on-screen text.
Keep motion slow and continuous.
Roll into the credits bar.
timing: Closing beats of 7 to 20 s before or under the credits.
loom_notes: A storyboard and script choice; recap and quiz templates exist if the question should also be answered. For corporate use the invitation becomes a reflection prompt or next action.

name: Deliberate ghost of the outgoing image
description: A low-opacity copy of the outgoing scene or figure stays visible over the incoming one: briefly, for the first moment of a cut between related beats so it feels continuous, or for a whole shot as meaning (a threat still hanging over a calm scene, a future or imagined state of the same characters).
when_to_use: An argument's turn, a threat that persists, a daydream or future state; or softening cuts in debates and stories where consecutive shots share subject or place.
how_to_execute: Cut or dissolve to the new scene as usual.
For a softened cut, overlay the previous frame at low opacity for the first moment and fade it out quickly, only between shots that share subject or place.
For a held ghost, keep the previous scene or figure at roughly a third opacity on the opposite third, with the new focal mass on the other third to balance.
Fade the held ghost out by the end of the shot.
timing: Softening ghosts last only the first frames or first beat; held ghosts persist for the full shot (0.6 to 5.6 s in the cited shots); fade-in median about 0.54 s.
loom_notes: Fade joins exist, but Loom's double-exposure-at-joins check would flag this deliberate device; record it as a conflict to resolve with an explicit, opt-in ghost join (short or held), not as a defect of the films.

name: Overhead flat-lay or top-down drift
description: A top-down view flattens a table, floor, room, garden or diorama into a diagram-like layout: as a short insert isolating one hand action or a symmetric arrangement, or as a slow drift over many repeated small figures and props to show scale or a whole environment at once.
when_to_use: One process step, a ritual or rule as a readable layout, a milestone; or the scale of a loss, a whole environment, where interruptions come from.
how_to_execute: Lay props flat on one plane, symmetric or on a clear grid, or scatter repeated small elements with seeded placement.
Reserve one accent for the exception.
For an insert, enter one hand or figure for the single action and stamp a date or label if the moment is a milestone.
For a drift, pan slowly and keep the elements still.
timing: Inserts of 0.8 to 9.6 s; overhead drifts of 4.4 to 10.2 s.
loom_notes: The overhead shot size and seeded arrays exist; tabletop object sets and top-down room art may need assets.

name: Slow pan or parallax drift over a still illustration
description: A static, wide illustration comes alive through one slow pan, truck or parallax drift across two or three depth layers while the figures stay still; any label stays fixed while the background moves beneath it.
when_to_use: Historical or establishing scenes, wide panoramas, labelled maps where the label must stay put.
how_to_execute: Paint the scene wider than the frame in two or three depth layers.
Drift slowly in one direction with an eased start and stop.
Hold any label fixed in screen space while the background moves beneath it.
timing: Pans and trucks of 2 to 15 s; pan right in 7 films of one batch.
loom_notes: Pan with parallax over depth layers exists; TED-Ed density backgrounds need imported assets.

name: A filled shape grows past the frame and its colour becomes the next field
description: At the end of a shot a flat filled shape (the finished subject, a badge, a dot, or a plain circle or rising panel) scales up until it covers the frame, and the next shot opens on a field of exactly that colour, so the figure itself is the join and no seam shows.
when_to_use: Flat graphic and diagram styles that change field colour between beats and should never show a seam; resets the eye with pure shape between topics.
how_to_execute: Hold the finished subject static for a beat, optionally flagged by a dashed ring.
Pick the next scene's field colour as the shape's fill (or grow a plain circle or rising panel in that colour).
Scale it with an ease-in from its point until its fill covers the frame.
Open the next shot on that same flat colour and begin the next diagram from the centre.
timing: Scale-in median about 0.8 to 0.9 s (p25 0.58 s); wipe shots 0.6 to 1.0 s.
loom_notes: Canvas, zoom and iris joins come close; the incoming station's field colour must be bound to the outgoing shape's fill as a join parameter.

name: Particles scatter or gather into the next shape
description: An object or word dissolves into fragments that drift and re-form into the next concept, or many identical units fall and gather into a word, formula or symbol, so data becomes a symbol and a term reads as a material rather than as type.
when_to_use: Turning one idea into the next without a cut; raw data becoming a symbol; introducing a technical name for a substance or a system made of many units.
how_to_execute: Isolate the source object on a flat or pale near-flat field.
Break it into fragments in the accent colour, or drop one repeated unit shape.
Drift the fragments along short paths into the target letterforms or outline.
Finish the build exactly as the name is spoken.
Mark completion with a thin ring pulse or add the label, then hold.
timing: Particle medians 1.58 to 2.46 s (p75 3.0 to 4.5 s); full beats 4 to 6.6 s; a formula build fills a 9.6 s shot (QWCHnR53oIw).
loom_notes: Particles exist; sampling target points from a glyph or outline so particles land on a shape is the missing parameter.

name: Stamp slam on the verdict word
description: A rubber stamp, woodblock emblem, year or rule slams onto the figure or page on the verdict word with a scale-in from slightly larger and a hard stop, slightly rotated, in the reserved accent colour, sometimes replacing a light script version of the same phrase.
when_to_use: Verdicts, approvals, rejections, risks, dates, rules hardening, withheld information, punchlines.
how_to_execute: Hold the subject or background still.
Scale the stamp in from slightly larger to a hard stop with a quick settle.
Rotate it a few degrees.
Use the accent colour only for the stamp.
Fade the layer behind if the stamp should carry the beat.
timing: Pop or stamp arrival p25 0.17 to 0.3 s, median 0.4 to 0.5 s.
loom_notes: Stamp motion exists.

name: Map route or region grows to the named place
description: On a muted two-tone map one accent route line draws itself as a curve, or a dark region spreads in small stepped increments, and the arrowhead or the region completes exactly as the destination is named; failed advances get X marks and a reversed row of arrows.
when_to_use: Journeys, redirections, rollouts, expansion and retreat, migrations, risks spreading across regions, flows between places.
how_to_execute: Flatten the map to two muted tones with thin labels.
Draw the route as one continuous curve, or grow the region one step per clause, in the accent colour only.
Time the arrowhead or the last step to the destination word.
Pop a disc or marker at the destination after arrival.
Mark stops with X stamps and show a reversal with a row of opposite arrows.
timing: Draw-on median 1.0 s, path-follow median 2.5 s (p75 4.0 s); a stepped region grow runs 6.8 s in about fifteen steps (NEFmWclWiOw s022); map shots run up to 10.8 s (uBwkMc1llmM s028).
loom_notes: Real geography, draw-on with arrowheads and travel along paths exist; a stepped region-fill animation is the missing parameter.

name: Picture and cause first, label and result after
description: The visual or the causing action is fully established first (the clog shown, the dial turned, the arrows aligned, the split complete) and the naming label, number or result appears only after it settles, so the word lands on an image the viewer already recognises and cause visibly precedes effect.
when_to_use: Technical terms, numbers, mechanisms and any cause-and-effect claim.
how_to_execute: Show the mechanism or object, or animate the cause in small eased steps.
Wait until it completes and settles.
Slide, type or pop the label or effect in on its term.
Keep the label off the subject.
Hold so the pairing reads.
timing: Labels follow the visual within the same shot; fade-in median 0.5 s, rotate median 1.5 s; a dial turns in eased steps, then pops follow within a 5.8 s shot (BlK23YzqXOM s020).
loom_notes: Cue order in the storyboard handles it; the motion vocabulary covers it.

name: Fast montage in the opening
description: The first 15 to 30 s cut fast through reactions, the phenomenon or the peril to make the stakes felt, then the film settles into its explanatory rhythm.
when_to_use: Openings that must make the stakes felt before the explanation.
how_to_execute: Pick five to thirteen short beats of the phenomenon or peril.
Cut them at about 0.6 to 3 s each.
Land on the question card or the first explanation.
Then lengthen the shots.
timing: HDt_rTPPh70 cuts 13 shots between 14.6 and 31.6 s; 6hCo4S_1Fhw runs 2.2 to 2.8 s shots between 16 and 31 s.
loom_notes: Cuts and shot timing are free; the pacing gate must allow a short-shot opening.

name: Stamp or strike a verdict onto a claim
description: An evaluation becomes a physical mark: a tilted, rough-edged stamp, a prohibition symbol or a starburst slams over a word, document or portrait on the key word, or a name is struck through by the same hand as the next name arrives, or a red X is painted over a rejected option.
when_to_use: Fact-checking a claim, marking something unreliable, approved, banned or rejected; several names for one thing.
how_to_execute: Show the claim first as a word, document or framed portrait, and hold it long enough to read.
On the key word, snap the stamp in with a fast pop and slight overshoot, tilted, overlapping the claim; or strike the old name with one stroke.
Write the next name beside or over a struck one.
Use the accent colour for the stamp or strike only.
Hold after the impact; no secondary motion beyond a gentle paper sway.
timing: pop_in median 0.58 s; each name 2 to 4 s inside an 18.7 s card.
loom_notes: Stamp and draw-on exist; needs a strike-through helper and a rough-edged stamp shape per pack.

name: One big number or year on a plain field
description: A single statistic or year is set large in the vacated centre of a plain field, beside at most one icon; a rolling counter locks on the spoken value, or a year pops on the spoken year in one reserved time colour and then dissolves into the next era's scene.
when_to_use: Single statistics (speed, a count, a percentage); era changes in history, company milestones and regulation timelines.
how_to_execute: Clear or exit the previous subject first.
Set the number large (height 0.08 to 0.35 of frame) in the film's style, beside one icon if any.
Roll the digits and lock on the spoken value, or pop the year on the spoken year.
Use one reserved colour for all time markers.
Pop a burst or accent only after the lock; then dissolve to the next scene.
timing: Year shots 0.6 to 1.4 s; counter shots about 4 s; number height median 0.08 (p75 0.18, p90 0.22) of frame.
loom_notes: Counters and title cards exist; a flip-odometer counter style is a parameter.

name: One accented line, dot or signal travels a fixed path
description: A route, flow, spread or signal is the only accented element: a ribbon that grows along a path toward a destination, a dot or vehicle moving on a top-down map, a dashed route drawn in travel order, or one bright pulse hopping node to node through a dim network; the same line can recur across scenes and change colour at the end state.
when_to_use: Routes, journeys, flows through a network, data moving through a system, risk approaching an asset, pipelines and spread.
how_to_execute: Mute the landscape, map, body or network (thin lines, pale nodes, dark tinted field).
Move one saturated element along the path: grow a ribbon, move a marker, draw a dashed stroke, or hop a glow between nodes.
Add faint secondary flickers elsewhere to keep a network alive.
Draw hidden or imagined things as dashed outlines and morph to solid when they become real.
Change the line's colour at the end state; end at the named destination.
Reuse the same ribbon in later scenes to keep the subject continuous.
timing: path_follow median 1.7 to 1.79 s (p90 3.96 s; code); draw_on median 0.75 s (p90 2.04 s); ribbon and map shots 5 to 15 s.
loom_notes: Travel along paths, draw-on, glow and maps exist; dashed strokes exist in the kit (stroke-dasharray on lines and paths, checked by grep). A dashed-to-solid state on objects would be a parameter.

name: Circular magnifier inset tied to the spot
description: A circular lens pops in over a held macro scene, tied to the exact spot by a thin leader line or pointer tail, showing the micro detail with both levels in frame; its content cross-fades between sub-views as the narration moves instead of cutting.
when_to_use: Showing a cell, a part, a metric or an internal process without leaving the context.
how_to_execute: Hold the macro scene static and slightly muted.
Draw a thin leader line from the named spot outward.
Pop the circular inset at its end with a springy scale.
Show the detail, or a comparison, inside it.
Cross-fade the inset content per sub-idea.
Pop the inset out when the sentence ends.
timing: scale_in median 0.7 to 0.8 s, exit_scale median 0.92 s (code); inset shots 4.2 to 15.8 s.
loom_notes: Insets can be composed from a clipped group and a line, and the iris join supplies the circle mask. A magnifier component (clip circle, leader line, nested content slot that cross-fades) is not listed. A true live magnification of the same scene needs the scene drawn twice under a clip, which SVG allows but no builder does today. The cross-fades may trip the double-exposure check.

name: Collapse the picture to a point or line, rebuild from it
description: Instead of a cut, the current composition clears itself: the figure or diagram folds into one dot, ring or vertical line (or scatters into particles, or slides off), the point holds as a visual full stop, and the next subject grows out of the same point.
when_to_use: Chapter turns and topic changes inside one visual register, where nothing of the old picture should remain except its focal point.
how_to_execute: Clear secondary elements first.
Collapse the subject toward its centre with an ease-out, or scatter it into particles.
Hold the dot, line or empty field briefly, up to about a second.
Grow the next subject out of the same point on the key word.
timing: Collapse beats 0.6 to 2.6 s shots; exit-scale median about 0.42 s; holds of the empty field about 1 s.
loom_notes: Scale, settle, particles and exits exist; a collapse-to-point join that hands its point to the next station needs a join parameter. The empty-field hold is a deliberate rest beat that the empty-frame check should accept.

name: Cut to a close insert on the key gesture
description: From a wide establishing frame the film hard-cuts to a close insert exactly when the key gesture or object matters (a card handed over, a blocked passenger, an unfinished line on paper, a laptop screen), holds it only while the object is named, then returns.
when_to_use: Making one object or action legible inside a larger scene.
how_to_execute: Establish the wide with the actor and object visible.
Cut to the insert as the gesture begins.
Hold the insert only while the object is named.
Cut back to the wide or on to the next beat.
timing: Inserts are brief; close and insert shots are 39 of 529 shot records in one batch.
loom_notes: Insert and close shot sizes exist; the UI artefacts (mail, chat, document) make screen inserts legible with real words.

name: Full-frame colour, inversion or grain beat as punctuation
description: A sub-second full-frame event marks a story beat without a new image: a red wash or white overexposure flashes on an arrival or shock, the palette inverts (dark to light, figure to X-ray) for one frame or is held to mark a turn, or a burst of grain in the film's palette sits between two scenes so a hard cut lands as a beat.
when_to_use: Shock or arrival beats, a change of heart or reversal, a jump from one person to the whole population, a scene turn in grim or textured lessons, or a reset between two registers. Use rarely.
how_to_execute: Hold the shot composition.
Flood the frame with one saturated colour or white, invert the field and ink, or cut to a full-frame grain field, for a short beat on the key word.
For a held inversion, change the pose at the same moment so the turn reads as meaning, not effect.
Drain back to the scene palette, or cut or expand into the next scene.
timing: Colour change median about 0.6 s (p25 0.33 s); flash shots 0.8 to 1.0 s; grain beats 0.6 to 1.0 s; a held inversion can last a whole 12 s shot.
loom_notes: The dip join with the shock meaning covers the flash; a pack-aware inversion (swap field and ink tokens) and a texture-only join using the shader grain layer are not named joins today.

name: A soft glow blooms on activation
description: A soft radial bloom with a bright core grows behind or on a static object at the moment it is named or activated (a card glows, a node lights, a molecule emits, a wall ignites), then holds, pulses gently or fades back to show a return to normal.
when_to_use: Activation, emission, insight, importance, the moment an idea appears.
how_to_execute: Keep the object static and simple, often a line drawing.
Grow a soft bloom with a bright core and soft edge, not a hard shape.
Peak the bloom on the spoken word.
Hold, pulse gently, or fade back to plain.
timing: Light-change median 1.0 s (p25 0.38 s, p75 2.54 s); an emission bloom fades out over about 1.8 s (P8OEz3PvWZQ s029).
loom_notes: Shader-layer glow and light effects exist (glow-flat).

name: A mechanism turns slowly and evenly
description: A dial, gear train or drum rotates slowly and evenly, so the motion reads as a mechanism rather than a flourish, and linked parts build to a synchronised climax when the whole system runs.
when_to_use: Explaining any machine, cycle or repeating process.
how_to_execute: Rotate at one slow, even rate.
Mesh linked parts at matching rates.
Mark moving parts with small saturated beads.
Add a light bloom when the full system runs together.
timing: Rotate median 4.6 s (p75 6.2 s, p90 9.0 s), seen in 6 films of batch 04. The evenness is as the records describe it; the code's own move-shape labels are not used here.
loom_notes: Rotation is a basic tween; meshed gear trains need a small builder.

name: Wordless near-still release beat
description: After a busy idea or before the credits, the narration drops and a calm, centred, often desaturated or minimal picture holds almost motionless, with one ambient loop or one small element (a falling leaf, a point of light) landing on the last spoken word, so the feeling lands.
when_to_use: Endings, lessons that close on an open question or reflection, emotional turns, after an overload sequence.
how_to_execute: Drop the narration, or let the last word land first.
Desaturate or simplify the image and centre a calm subject.
Hold it nearly still with one ambient loop.
Time one small element to land on the last spoken word.
Then cut to the credits or the next idea.
timing: Holds of about 10 to 18 s (UQdtUaeZWLo s018b 10.2 s, jG7ULeWUfDw s039 11.1 s, 56F0Y33QZnQ s069 18.4 s); HDt_rTPPh70 runs nine wordless shots from 273.2 to 288.2 s.
loom_notes: Holds, ambient loops and word timing exist. Conflict to resolve: static-hold and empty-frame lints, and the judge model, tend to flag these deliberate holds.

name: A new flat field colour for each new idea
description: Each short idea sits on its own single flat saturated field with no environment (lavender, yellow, red, green; pink stage, green pitch, cream oven), so a new idea is signalled by a new field while the drawing language and accent stay constant. Faster than a section colour script: the field changes per beat, not per chapter.
when_to_use: Diagram-led, object-led, abstract or psychological films with many short distinct ideas and no natural setting.
how_to_execute: Pick a field sequence from the pack's range (often a warm set).
Place only the subject and one prop on the field.
Keep one accent hue constant across fields, reserved for the special element.
Change field only on a new idea, never inside one, by a shape fill, wipe or hard cut.
timing: One field per beat; beats of 0.6 to 4.8 s in one film and 2 to 17 s in another.
loom_notes: Station backgrounds are settable and close to presenter-pop; a pack-level field-colour cycle parameter would make it systematic.

name: The keyword becomes an object or a picture of itself
description: A key word on screen is acted on physically to show its meaning: loops weave through its letters, it is re-stamped heavier, smudges into an ink blot, cracks and is rebuilt stitched, is torn in two, a figure's body is built from it, the camera flies into a letter, or an object morphs into the word it names.
when_to_use: Defining one abstract word, or naming the core concept of a section so label and subject are one element.
how_to_execute: Set the word large on a flat field at the cut and hold it about 3 s so it is read.
Spend the motion on the idea, not the entrance.
Apply one physical change to the letters (weave, restamp, blot, crack, tear, build into a body, open into a space).
Land the change on the spoken payoff word.
Hand the transformed word into the next diagram rather than cutting.
timing: Word holds about 3 s before transforming; push into a letter in a 0.8 s shot; one weave draws on in a single ease-in-out pass inside a 3.0 s shot.
loom_notes: Text and draw-on exist; needs text converted to editable outlines with letter-level masks that can crack, split, weave over and under, and morph into shapes.

name: Loose single-stroke line as the whole language
description: Everything is drawn in one loose, wobbly single-stroke line with light hatching and visible overdraw and no clean vector edges, which keeps clinical or political subjects informal and human.
when_to_use: Human, low-stakes or reflective topics where warmth matters more than precision.
how_to_execute: Use one line weight family for all foreground strokes.
Add a stroke jitter so lines are uneven but stable between frames.
Hatch lightly for shadow; avoid fills except washes.
Keep the line identical across every vignette.
timing: Not time-based; outline coded sketchy in 157 shots across 11 films of one batch.
loom_notes: line-art draws clean strokes; a static per-stroke jitter parameter is buildable, true frame-to-frame line boil is not possible.

name: Same figure, new state, morphed in place
description: A change of state or behaviour (asleep to awake, tense to calm, child to adult, crouch to sprint) is shown by morphing or pose-swapping the same figure in its place, never by cutting to a new character; position, colours and silhouette identity stay fixed.
when_to_use: Before and after, growth, recovery, a change of role, and behaviours told by the whole body.
how_to_execute: Keep position, colours and silhouette identity fixed.
Key two or three poses or states.
Swap the pose or morph the shape over about a second.
Add one supporting cue: a background temperature shift, a hue wash or a halo bloom.
Hold each state briefly; optionally close the film by reversing roles with the same figure.
timing: Morph median 0.71 to 1.17 s (p90 2.67 s; code); colour change median 0.92 s; held poses sit in 1.0 to 4.4 s shots.
loom_notes: Rig pose swaps exist and are the nearest equivalent. An organic body morph (aging, one blob reshaping between poses) is listed as not possible today and would need a shape-morph primitive.

name: Rings from a source act on what they touch
description: Thin concentric arcs pulse out from a single source in one reserved colour; objects pop in or recolour only when a ring reaches them, tying the change to a visible cause, and the rings flatten or collapse when the idea settles.
when_to_use: Invisible signals, sound, scanning, detection, attention, the reach of a message.
how_to_execute: Reserve one accent colour for the signal only.
Place the source on a plain or dark field.
Emit two to four thin rings that expand and fade.
Reveal or recolour each object when a ring crosses it.
Flatten, stop or collapse the rings to a small circle when the narration resolves.
timing: grow median 1.5 s (code); ring shots 1.6 to 11 s.
loom_notes: Rings can be drawn and particles and ambient drift exist. Needs a ring emitter and a timing helper that computes when the ring radius reaches each object.

name: Node-and-line network built hub first
description: Relationships are pale nodes joined by thin lines: the subject sits in a hub circle, nodes pop in a stagger on the naming words, connectors draw only after every node is present, and the symbol on a link can swap to change the relationship type while one node fills with the accent for the decision-maker.
when_to_use: Functions of one system, roles, stakeholder maps, ownership and approval links, a mid-film or end recap.
how_to_execute: Start with a small legible cluster: the hub in a large circle.
Pop the nodes in a stagger on the spoken list.
Draw connectors only after all nodes are present.
Swap link symbols in place without moving nodes.
Fill one node with the accent at the decision; grow in a second wave if the network scales.
timing: Staggered pops in a 3 s shot; network shots 6 to 19 s; one web builds over 12.4 s.
loom_notes: Icon grid and recap templates, pops and draw-on lines cover a static build. A node-link builder with link-symbol slots would make swaps and second waves reusable.

name: Slide carousel of examples inside a fixed frame
description: The old picture slides off one edge while the next slides in from the opposite edge, inside a border or frame that stays fixed, so examples read as one sequence.
when_to_use: Enumerating examples, vignettes or evidence items of the same kind.
how_to_execute: Fix a border or frame and the field colour.
Slide the current vignette out horizontally as the next slides in.
Pop in each new figure or label only when named.
End on the simplest symbol of the set.
timing: Slide-in and exit-slide medians about 0.67 s.
loom_notes: Travel join and slide motions exist; keep the frame layer outside the travelling layer.

name: Whole film inside one hue family
description: The film stays in one hue family (pink, red-pink, black and white, paper and ink), varying only value and saturation per section, so even hard cuts feel like one world and the single off-family accent carries all emphasis.
when_to_use: Single-system topics (one body, one process, one story) where continuity matters more than variety.
how_to_execute: Choose the family from the subject (body interior, paper sketch, black void).
Vary value and saturation inside the family per section, not hue.
Reserve one off-family accent for danger, the active element or the key object.
timing: Holds for the whole film; section shifts are value shifts.
loom_notes: A pack palette can do this; the design seed needs a one-family option so lessons do not drift across hues.

name: Glow halo instead of an outline
description: Flat, unstroked shapes are separated from a saturated or dark field by a soft halo or a thin light ring rather than a dark outline; a stronger glow marks the active element.
when_to_use: Outline-free styles on saturated or dark fields where shapes would otherwise merge.
how_to_execute: Draw the shape with no stroke.
Add a soft outer glow in a lighter tint of the field, or a thin light ring.
Use a stronger glow only on the active element.
timing: Static styling; active-element glow pulses follow light_change timing (median 0.79 s).
loom_notes: glow-flat provides halos and the shader glow.

name: One thin weather or mood particle layer
description: One thin, pale layer of falling rain streaks, snow, embers, petals or tears runs across every depth plane at one angle and speed, setting the mood and keeping a held frame alive; its density can track the intensity of a feeling.
when_to_use: Tension, weather, stress, grief, overload, a building storm, the passage of time.
how_to_execute: Choose one particle type that belongs to the story.
Draw it thin and pale, low contrast against the field.
Run it across every plane at one angle and speed, through held shots.
Keep the figure static or walking slowly; raise density with the narration's intensity.
timing: particle median 2.0 s per burst (p75 3.0 s); ambient loops median 3.8 s; a storm builds over about 10 s; rain held over a 17.0 s cross-section.
loom_notes: Particles and ambient drift exist.

name: Small workers each do one literal job to a central object
description: A multi-step or multi-actor process is told as small figures, each performing one literal action per narration clause (heat, pour, scrub, signal with a horn, march as defenders) on a single central object that transforms in place after each step.
when_to_use: Procedures, approvals, team workflows, manufacturing, and invisible processes with several distinct actors.
how_to_execute: Split the narration into clauses, one actor per clause.
Centre the object and keep it there for the whole sequence.
Bring in one small figure per step, each with one prop that names its job.
Animate only that job, repeated; transform the object in place after the step.
Put the accent only on the decisive change; label each actor with a word in the world's material.
timing: Worker shots 1.4 to 7.4 s; whole sequences 11.2 to 16.1 s.
loom_notes: Rigs and hold-and-transform exist separately; a recipe pairing one gesture per step with an object state change does not, and a small cast with job props is an asset task. For corporate workflows, role figures with one tool each fit better than creatures.

name: Name label or card on the spoken name
description: A person is identified by a label, badge or nameplate that pops in beside the face as the name is spoken and clears once established; a stronger variant stamps the held pose into a printed artefact (a card with a nameplate banner) to mark a role.
when_to_use: Introducing an expert, a historical figure, a protagonist or a case-study person; marking a role change.
how_to_execute: Frame tight on the face or hold the character's pose.
Pop the label beside the shoulder, never over the face, on the spoken name.
For the card variant, cut to the same pose inside a card frame and stamp the frame and nameplate on the name, with a slow push-in.
Clear the label once established; pull back to the full figure if needed.
timing: pop_in median 0.4 s, exit_fade median 0.54 s (code), inside 1.4 to 10.4 s shots; a card push-in over 3 to 4 s.
loom_notes: Text labels, pops and stamps exist; a card or nameplate frame template would standardise the card variant. Names must come from the source.

name: Identical frames that differ in one variable
description: Two or four identical framed vignettes sit side by side; only the variable under test changes, effect icons pop above and labels below, and a gesture concludes (one frame slides away, the rejected cause is struck, a scale tips). The same grid shows 'it varies' by demoting the hero to one tile among variants, and 'it is universal' by one gesture played in sync across differently coloured cells.
when_to_use: Debunking, before and after, two plans, variation across people or teams, universality of a behaviour.
how_to_execute: Build one vignette and duplicate it into equal frames, same crop and outline weight.
Change only the variable under test in one frame.
Pop small effect icons above each, then category labels below.
