Resolve with a gesture: slide one frame away and strike the rejected cause, or tip toward the winner.
For variation, shrink the subject into a corner tile and pop the variants in staggered waves.
For universality, animate the same gesture in every cell at once.
timing: Whole beat 5 to 16 s; pops median 0.46 s each (code).
loom_notes: Split layouts, icon grids, stamps, staggered groups and draw-on strike-through exist.

name: Morph the model in place, labels attached
description: A diagram reorganises in place (a tree into braided lines, an expected bar into the actual bar, an isometric model flattening into its own plan) while labelled elements stay attached and trackable, so a misconception is corrected or a new view revealed without a cut.
when_to_use: Correcting a misconception, revealing a surprising result, moving between views of a layered design (architecture, org layers).
how_to_execute: Show the familiar or expected version and hold it so it is believed.
Keep labels attached to their nodes.
Morph the structure in one continuous move on the correcting word.
Hold the corrected version still as fact; step a highlight through layers if they matter.
timing: Expected state held several seconds, then one morph (morph median 1.38 s; code) in 7.8 to 8.2 s shots.
loom_notes: Bar height morphs are chart tweens and exist. Arbitrary diagram restructuring with tracked nodes, and an isometric-to-plan transform, need a layout-morph primitive.

name: Dissolve through a shared colour between media or worlds
description: A fade through a colour taken from the outgoing flat scene, or a diagonal colour band wipe, bridges flat graphics and very different material (live or archival footage), with the incoming material tinted toward that hue and masked inside the graphic language.
when_to_use: Switching between illustration and footage, or between two very different worlds.
how_to_execute: Pick the dominant colour of the outgoing flat scene.
Tint the incoming material toward the same hue.
Join with a short fade through that colour or a diagonal band wipe.
Mask the incoming material (circle or band) so it sits inside the graphic language.
timing: Fade-in median about 0.54 s; one fade-through-colour shot 1.8 s.
loom_notes: A dip through a chosen colour exists; tinting footage needs a footage source and the shader layer, which Loom does not draw. Usable as-is between two code-drawn packs.

name: Impact burst as punctuation and as a reveal
description: A starburst, scalloped impact cloud or radiating line burst scales in on a hit or shock and then bursts apart or shrinks to expose the next scene, so the transition itself means disruption.
when_to_use: Shocks, disruptions, overwhelming feelings, the key moment in a panel.
how_to_execute: Build the burst from flat radiating lines or a scalloped cloud in one colour.
Scale it in fast on the beat.
Optionally fill it with tumbling small figures.
Burst it apart or shrink it to expose the next scene.
timing: Scale-in median about 0.58 s; burst-to-reveal about 1 to 2 s in the cited shots.
loom_notes: Stamp, pop and the shock meaning exist; needs a burst shape preset that can act as a matte for the join.

name: An ambiguous shape resolves into the object on its first noun
description: A glowing blob, a light streak or an abstract field is held as a question, then resolves into the real object as the narration first names it, so the subject is revealed rather than cut to.
when_to_use: Opening a metaphor, or bridging an abstract quantity to its physical subject.
how_to_execute: Start with a simple warm shape or streak in a dark field.
Hold it long enough to read as a question.
Morph it into the object on the spoken noun.
Keep the accent on the same part across the morph.
timing: Blob held about 2.6 s, then a 2.6 s morph shot in one film; a streak-to-train resolve over 9.8 s in another; morph median about 1.0 s.
loom_notes: Needs the same path-morph primitive as outline_morph_join; an unmask or draw-on from a glow is a reachable approximation.

name: Scroll unroll or page turn reveal
description: A scroll unrolls or a page corner peels to reveal a map or the next diagram, often using an object from the previous scene as the mechanism, then a year or title is stamped once the surface is flat.
when_to_use: History beats, chapter turns, or any reveal of a map or document.
how_to_execute: Show the closed scroll or page as an object first.
Unroll or peel it along one axis.
Fade or slide the content in as the surface opens.
Stamp a year or title once the surface is flat.
timing: Unfold median about 1.4 s (p25 0.71 s, p75 1.79 s).
loom_notes: No page-curl or scroll-unroll primitive; the document object has states but not a curl.

name: A character redraws into the object of its state
description: A figure redraws itself, whole or in part, into the thing it is experiencing or becoming (a face into a struggling mouth, a head into a brain, a child into a warrior), making an internal state or a link between eras literal.
when_to_use: Making an internal state, or a link between two eras, the literal object of the explanation, often at the hook.
how_to_execute: Frame the character close and centred.
Hold the pose until the keyword.
Morph the whole figure or one part into the metaphor object on the word.
Let new props sketch in only after the figure has settled.
timing: Fast and snappy at the hook; transform-into median 0.96 s.
loom_notes: Organic frame-by-frame figure morphs are on Loom's not-possible list; the nearest approximation is a cross-dissolve plus scale on a shared anchor point, which will read differently.

name: Secondary particles only at peaks
description: Sweat drops, sparkles, confetti and small bursts appear only at emotional or magical peaks as punctuation, never continuously.
when_to_use: Panic, celebration, recognition, the moment of an award or a reveal.
how_to_execute: Find the peak word of the beat.
Emit a small burst of a few particles at the subject.
Let them drift out and clear.
Keep the rest of the shot free of particles.
timing: Particle median 1.5 s (p25 0.6 s, p75 2.42 s).
loom_notes: Particles exist and can be cued to a word; a peak-word trigger preset would make it a one-line choice.

name: Slow colour wash over a static drawing
description: The drawing never changes; only a tint creeps over it from one area or the whole frame (grey to blood red, cool to hot), making an invisible internal process visible.
when_to_use: Infection, heat, stress, risk building, or any internal change with no visible shape.
how_to_execute: Draw the scene once, fully, in the base palette.
Start a tint from one area or the whole frame.
Grow its strength slowly in step with the narration.
Stop at full strength on the key word.
timing: Colour change median 1.5 s (p75 3.4 s, p90 9.0 s); light change median 2.0 s.
loom_notes: The shader layer and colour tokens exist; a timed scene tint and a whole-environment colour temperature shift are parameters to add.

name: Long testimony holds with short illustrated bursts
description: Long locked holds on a live speaker alternate with short illustrated bursts for each metaphor, and the pace quickens at section markers with comic cards.
when_to_use: Multi-voice expert or employee films.
how_to_execute: Hold the live speaker while the point is made.
Cut to a short illustrated burst for the metaphor.
Return to the speaker.
Speed up at section markers with comic cards.
timing: Testimony holds 8 to 17 s (zrjhaYc-9pg s032 12.8 s; 2x3rJMBVB28 s048 14.4 s); bursts 1.0 to 3.8 s (zrjhaYc-9pg s033 1.0 s).
loom_notes: Depends on live interview footage, which Loom cannot shoot; it would need imported footage, while the illustrated bursts are within reach.

name: Cool actor inside a saturated warm interior world
description: Inside-the-body or micro scenes flood the field with a saturated red, pink or warm monochrome with thin branching contour lines, and the active agent is the only cool blue or cyan element; passive elements stay white or pale. The film re-enters this same interior palette each time the process continues.
when_to_use: Any invisible internal process (infection, signalling, data moving inside a system) that needs its own recognisable space.
how_to_execute: Flood the field with one warm hue plus thin branching or wavy contour lines for texture.
Draw the agent in cool blue with a dark outline and a simple face.
Keep defenders or passive elements in white or pale tones.
Return to the same interior palette every time the process continues.
timing: Interior beats run 2 to 15 s; the world is re-entered several times per film.
loom_notes: The inside-a-body place and glow-flat colours cover the world; the agent character needs assets.

name: Grey live footage, saturated flat overlays
description: Live interview footage is graded toward grey and all saturated colour belongs to flat cartoon overlays popped beside the face, so the graphics read as the idea and the person as the voice.
when_to_use: Expert or employee testimony with illustrated emphasis.
how_to_execute: Lock the camera on a centred medium shot.
Desaturate the footage.
Pop saturated flat overlays on keywords beside the face.
Clear them before the next idea.
timing: Overlays pop at pop_in median 0.5 s; testimony holds 8 to 17 s.
loom_notes: Loom does not film or composite live footage today; with consented clips it needs a desaturate grade and an overlay layer.

name: Hazy depth planes from flat shapes
description: Exteriors are built from two or three flat planes of one shape vocabulary (pale far, mid, dark foreground framer) in a narrow desaturated range with a white haze, so the scene reads as atmosphere rather than detail.
when_to_use: Establishing shots and story openings, to set mood without drawing detail.
how_to_execute: Draw three planes of the same shape vocabulary (trunks, hills, buildings).
Lift the far plane toward white; keep the foreground darkest.
Add a faint vertical gradient or haze band.
Let one figure in the accent colour cross the mid plane.
timing: Fade up from white about 0.5 s, then hold 3 to 6 s with ambient drift.
loom_notes: Depth layers with parallax exist; needs a per-plane haze tint and value ramp.

name: Era coded by palette plus a fixed date anchor
description: Historical sequences shift the whole palette (monochrome, sepia, cream) and keep a small year tag in a fixed corner across consecutive shots, a large date range across a split scene, or a year that pops on its mention, so time is anchored without captions.
when_to_use: History segments and time jumps.
how_to_execute: Choose an era palette distinct from the present.
Place a small year tag in a fixed corner across consecutive shots, or a large date range across a split scene.
Pop the year on its spoken mention.
Return to the present palette with a dissolve or a doorway of light.
timing: Year tag persists across 4 to 5 consecutive shots; pops median 0.46 s.
loom_notes: Text and palettes exist; needs a per-section palette override and a persistent corner tag across stations.

name: Threat larger and angular, protagonist small and round
description: Threats and pressures are drawn at least twice the protagonist's height, angular or spiky, or as dark silhouettes with one accent; the protagonist is small and round, so size and shape carry the power relation before any action.
when_to_use: Risks, pressures and antagonists: debt, a breach, a deadline, an overwhelming feeling.
how_to_execute: Draw the threat with pointed shapes and at least twice the protagonist's height.
Give it one accent (eyes or edges) and keep the body dark or white.
Slide it in or loom it from the edge, then act on the small figure.
Shrink or remove it when the problem is solved.
timing: Arrival slide median 0.67 s, exit slide median 0.79 s (code).
loom_notes: Shape language can be expressed in code-drawn objects, but threat characters need assets. For a corporate audience keep the threat abstract (a looming angular shape or object) and drop fangs and glowing eyes.

name: Negate a claim in place
description: A wrong claim stays visible as a label while a red strike-through, an ink blot or a bold X is drawn over it, with one short negation word above.
when_to_use: Myths, outdated rules, wrong theories, revised policies.
how_to_execute: Write the claim as a label and hold it for reading.
Draw the strike or blot on the spoken word that introduces the problem.
Add one short red negation word above; keep the original visible.
timing: Hold the first half of a 3.4 s shot, then draw_on (median 1.0 s; code).
loom_notes: Draw-on with a strike path and stamps cover it.

name: An abstract rule as one object doing one action
description: An abstract idea is a single familiar object performing one continuous action from start to finish (a drum drops a ball, a scroll unrolls, a sack overflows, a dial is pushed past a limit), isolated in a soft light pool or on a flat field, with one small accent marking the result.
when_to_use: Rules, selection, cost, limits and abstractions with no natural picture.
how_to_execute: Pick one familiar object whose action matches the idea.
Isolate it in a soft light pool or on a flat field.
Run exactly one action from start to finish on the narration.
Show the result with one small accent; no labels needed.
timing: Shots of 1.4 to 5.4 s.
loom_notes: Object grammars with states (document, clock, lock and others) exist; new objects need families.

name: A statistic with a small figure enacting it
description: A number about people is paired with one small character performing the behaviour it measures (lying awake, celebrating, carrying the percentage), so the data reads as a tiny scene.
when_to_use: Any statistic about people.
how_to_execute: Place the number large and central.
Add one small foreground figure enacting the measured behaviour.
Trigger the figure's action on the key spoken word.
Keep context props outline-only so they do not compete.
timing: Figure act median 0.5 s; number draw_on median 0.75 s (code).
loom_notes: Counters plus rig poses compose today. The number must trace to the source.

name: Chart builds band by band in narration order
description: A chart (stacked area, line on a dark field, tier bars, a timeline with a chart) builds one element at a time as each is named; the key change is encoded in the shape, and labels appear only when there is room.
when_to_use: Compounding, trends that change when a factor arrives, hierarchies, developmental sequences.
how_to_execute: Anchor the base with a story object, then remove it as data takes over.
Grow each band or draw each line segment after the previous is established.
Encode the key change in shape (the top band curves up, the line bends).
Fade labels in only once their area can hold the text; push in to reframe the curve as a direction.
timing: grow median 1.5 s per band; draw_on median 0.75 s (code); chart beats 6 to 8 s.
loom_notes: Charts that build exist; stacked area and dark-field line styling may need parameters. Data must come from the source.

name: Assemble the whole in the order the parts are named
description: An object or figure assembles from its parts in the exact order they are spoken (a kit, a face from tiles, a rocket from floating shapes), each snapping in with a small settle, with the user or the result arriving last.
when_to_use: What something is made of, or how parts combine into an outcome.
how_to_execute: Lay out the empty field or a faint silhouette of the whole.
Bring each part in on its spoken name, in reading order.
Snap parts with a small settle.
Bring the user or the result in last.
timing: One kit builds in a 6.4 s shot; one assembly spans a 17.0 s closing shot.
loom_notes: Staggered groups and settle exist.

name: Camera drifts through a crowded flat collage
description: A claim of ubiquity is made concrete by a dense, low-negative-space scatter of everyday objects that the camera slowly drifts through, with one tiny human for scale and a burst of the subject's particle motif at the end.
when_to_use: Hooks about ubiquity, hidden risk or volume (data everywhere, risk in every process).
how_to_execute: Scatter objects with slight seeded rotations and overlaps on one muted field.
Keep all the saturated warm colour on the objects.
Drift the camera slowly (push or tilt) without animating the objects.
Drop in one tiny figure among oversized objects.
End on a burst of the particle motif that stands for the subject.
timing: Drift held over 7 to 10 s shots; particle burst at the end of the shot.
loom_notes: Pan, push and parallax exist; a seeded scatter-collage layout with overlap and rotation is a layout parameter Loom lacks.

name: Dive from an illustrated set through its screen
description: A series opener: a layered, often symmetric illustrated studio with a central monitor; the screen resolves from abstract blocks into the presenter or first scene and the camera pushes through it, so the join reads as a focus shift. The same set returns at the end.
when_to_use: Series openers and expert-led lessons where a presenter should feel embedded in an illustrated world, or any time a busy context must narrow to one voice.
how_to_execute: Build a layered set: foreground desk, midground screen dead centre, background wall, matching elements either side, one warm accent on the screen.
Resolve the monitor content from abstract blocks into the presenter.
Push in with a slow ease-in for under 2 s, letting side props slide off frame as the camera advances.
Continue the move across the shot boundary until the screen fills the frame and resolves into the speaker or first scene.
Return to the same set for the ending to bookend (see callback_to_opening_image).
timing: Opening push 1.8 s then dive 1.4 s in one film (0 to 3.2 s); boot and dive 0 to 3.8 s across three shots in another; a two-shot push-in over 0 to 8 s in a third.
loom_notes: The zoom join into a nested station and depth-layer places exist; a studio set with a screen prop needs assets, and live-action footage plus its grading is not in Loom's capability list. A code-drawn rig presenter on the monitor is the reachable variant.

name: Magnifier slides in and its enlarged content becomes the next diagram
description: A magnifying glass slides in from off-screen, settles on the subject and shows an enlarged detail or scale reference inside the lens; the camera then trucks into the lens content so it becomes the next shot.
when_to_use: Moving from a simple surface (a symbol, a photo, a fragment) to the mechanism or detail behind it.
how_to_execute: Hold the whole scene still.
Slide the lens in from the frame edge with an ease-out and settle it on the subject.
Show the enlarged content inside the lens.
Push or truck into the revealed content so it becomes the next shot.
timing: Slide-in median about 0.8 s; the lens eases in and out to bookend a hold of about 2.6 s in one film.
loom_notes: Needs a lens component: a circular clip that shows a scaled copy of the layer beneath, plus a camera move into it.

name: One small figure in a vast mood image before the topic is named
description: The first narrated image is a single small figure, carrying the only accent colour, in a large near-monochrome, weather-filled or cold space, so the feeling arrives before the subject is named.
when_to_use: Topics with an emotional or human stake (wellbeing, change, loss, risk) where the viewer should feel the problem first.
how_to_execute: Place one small figure with the only accent colour in a large near-monochrome space.
Add one ambient system (rain strokes, drifting specks) over every layer.
Hold the camera static for 6 to 10 s while the narration sets the scene.
Name the topic only on the next beat.
timing: First narrated shots run 6.6 to 10.2 s with ambient loops (batch ambient loop median 3.8 s).
loom_notes: Depth-layer place plus particles and one accent token; keep the figure professional (no gore or horror register for employee audiences).

name: Forward plunge down a one-point perspective path or tunnel
description: The camera travels forward down a symmetric one-point perspective corridor, path or tunnel built from repeated flat shapes (trapezoids, gate frames, a glowing ribbon) toward a gate or vanishing point, and resolves on the next era or destination.
when_to_use: Era changes in a history, journeys and passage of time, arriving at a destination, moving into unfamiliar territory.
how_to_execute: Build the path or tunnel from stacked flat shapes converging on one vanishing point, with a gate or door at the end.
Keep one anchor figure static at an edge if needed.
Push forward with an ease-in for a plunge, or slowly for dread.
Arrive on the gate or the new era's establishing shot on the key word.
timing: About 1 s per tunnel segment (ease-in moves median about 0.83 s); a corridor travel of 1.6 s and a plunge of 2.6 s in one film.
loom_notes: Depth layers with parallax and push exist; there is no tunnel or corridor set builder. Buildable in SVG or a three.js clip.

name: Row of identical figures with offset loops
description: Many identical figures perform the same looping action slightly out of phase, so a row reads as collective, continuous labour or a stream of events.
when_to_use: The scale of manual effort, a crowd, a continuous stream of events.
how_to_execute: Draw one figure with small pose or hair variations.
Repeat it in a row or along a diagonal.
Offset each loop's phase.
Pan slowly across the row, or let actions travel off frame.
timing: Shots of 2.2 to 7.2 s; character-act median 1.0 s per loop.
loom_notes: Staggered groups and seeded arrays exist; set the phase offsets from the seed.

name: Counter lands on the spoken number
description: A rolling counter or a filling dot grid runs while the narrator approaches a figure and settles on the spoken value, then the readout often morphs into a map, route or orbit to give it scale.
when_to_use: Any quantity the learner should remember, especially rates, durations and totals.
how_to_execute: Place the counter as the hero of the frame with one accent box.
Start counting a beat before the number is spoken.
Land on the value on the spoken word and hold.
Morph the readout into a spatial view (map, route, orbit) to give it scale.
timing: Counter shot 8.4 s followed by an 11 s map shot (2A1IEBFt6Xg s060, s061); XNEHP6qFeCs s020b runs 18.3 s.
loom_notes: Counters and word timings exist; the counter-to-map handover needs real geography plus a join.

name: Expanding rings for a field or wireless link
description: Concentric rings pulse out from a source to show a magnetic field, a wireless signal or a sensing range acting at a distance, without wires or text.
when_to_use: Any force or connection that has no visible carrier.
how_to_execute: Place the source above or beside the target.
Pulse thin rings outward at a steady rate.
Change the target (glow, move) when the rings reach it.
timing: Ring diagrams hold 3 to 14 s (ul-c6a4QkiU s024 3.2 s; 2A1IEBFt6Xg s053 14 s).
loom_notes: A seeded ring emitter is a small builder over existing motion and particles.

name: Speed from streaks or scrolling, not from the camera
description: Speed is shown by scrolling background layers or directional streaks behind a fixed subject, never by moving the camera on a static subject; fast action is held as frozen dynamic poses against the streaks, and one film smears the whole frame into a horizontal blur whip to change topic.
when_to_use: Vehicles, chases, anything fast.
how_to_execute: Lock the camera and the subject.
Scroll background layers at different rates, or draw streaks in the direction of travel.
Blur the nearest layer most.
For action, hold the key pose of each beat against the streaks and cut every 1 to 3 s.
For a topic change, smear the whole frame horizontally over a few frames and cut in already moving.
timing: 2A1IEBFt6Xg s005 3.6 s; QFbQkZT1EEk s030 1.4 s; frozen-pose cuts 1.4 to 1.6 s (QFbQkZT1EEk s034, s035); the whip is sub-second.
loom_notes: Parallax depth layers exist; streak fields and per-layer scroll behind a fixed subject are parameters. Skia clips have motion blur but no join uses it.

name: Still subject, cycling sky or season palette
description: The subject holds still while the background palette cycles day to night or season to season, often with a sun and moon moving, compressing time into a few seconds.
when_to_use: Durations: waiting, digestion, years of confinement, round-the-clock work.
how_to_execute: Lock the subject and layout.
Animate the background hue (warm day to cool night) and a sun or moon position.
Cut through several short held states for a time lapse.
Keep one tiny secondary motion (an insect, a flicker) for life.
timing: Cycle cuts of 0.6 to 3.2 s each; light_change median 1.0 s.
loom_notes: Colour tweens exist; a background time-of-day ramp with sun and moon is a station parameter to add.

name: Clear the frame before the next idea
description: Inside one long shot, each mini-scene leaves completely (fade, shrink or lift out) before the next one enters, with a beat of empty field between, so the eye never tracks two ideas at once.
when_to_use: Dense lists of examples inside one long shot.
how_to_execute: Finish the current idea and hold briefly.
Exit every element (fade, shrink or lift out).
Show the empty field for a beat.
Bring the next idea in.
timing: exit_fade median 0.54 s; exit_scale median 0.83 s.
loom_notes: Exit motions and staggered groups exist. Loom's empty-frame check may flag the deliberate empty beat; record it as a gate conflict.

name: One 3D or photo element in a flat field
description: A single glossy 3D object, photoreal render or photo cutout is dropped into a flat 2D field and kept as an object on the field with a contact shadow or halftone halo, so the dimension contrast pulls the eye to the real thing.
when_to_use: Presenting the product or the physical thing the lesson is about.
how_to_execute: Keep the field flat and simple.
Drop in one dimensional element with a contact shadow or a halftone halo.
Never blend it into the drawing; keep it as an object on the field.
timing: Inserts held 3 to 19 s.
loom_notes: three.js clips can render one 3D prop; photo cutouts need licensed assets.

name: Text sits on a paper card, tag or band
description: On-screen text never floats loose: it appears on a flat paper card, bar, band, or a white tag with a folded corner and soft shadow dropped onto the region it names or held up by a hand.
when_to_use: Questions, lists of names and definitions in flat styles; naming parts of an internal process; making an abstract role a physical token.
how_to_execute: Slide a flat card up from the bottom edge, or drop a folded-corner tag onto the named region with a short arrow.
Fade the text in once the card settles, or pop list words onto a single bar one at a time.
Settle with an ease-out pop on the word.
timing: Card slide-in median 0.63 s; text fade median 0.58 s; tag pop and settle about 0.5 s.
loom_notes: Templates over scenes already get a backplate and document and card objects exist; a folded-corner tag variant is a small addition.

name: Labels in staggered waves with thin leader lines
description: Diagram labels arrive in two or more waves with thin drawn-on leader lines instead of all at once, so annotation reads as a calm build; a variant pops small label cards as each input is named, then draws a coloured stream from the label to its object.
when_to_use: Labelling a structure with more than three parts.
how_to_execute: Reveal the object first and let it settle.
Bring the first group of labels in with leader lines drawn on.
Pause, then bring the second group.
Glow the one or two labels that matter most at the end.
timing: One build runs 11.8 s; diagram text median height 0.03 of frame (p10 0.02), so check the reading floor.
loom_notes: Staggered groups plus draw-on leaders; enforce the 0.03 reading floor at render size.

name: Numbered list with one acting icon per item
description: A list item is a typed headline plus a large low-contrast corner numeral, illustrated by one small icon that draws on, performs one action and exits before the next; or a list of examples cross-fades in one identical centred frame with a small corner label.
when_to_use: Tips, triggers, tools or examples where the list itself is the content.
how_to_execute: Place a large low-contrast numeral in a corner as a watermark.
Type the headline on word by word with the narration.
Draw on one icon, let it act once, exit it in a consistent direction.
Keep the accent only on the active text and icon.
timing: Each item about 7 to 8 s (four tips span 30 s); exit_scale median 0.42 s.
loom_notes: The list template exists; it needs the corner numeral, per-item icon act-and-exit and word-timed typing.

name: Drawn bracket, ruler or multiplier on the spoken number
description: A quantified claim gets a drawn measurement mark (bracket plus number, protractor arc, vertical ruler, x4 multiplier) anchored to the picture, drawn on as the figure is spoken and then held for reading.
when_to_use: Any spoken number that compares sizes, angles, rates or multiples.
how_to_execute: Show the subject doing the thing first.
Draw the measurement mark on in one stroke as the number is said.
Write the number beside it in the lesson's label face.
Hold the frame so the measure can be read.
timing: draw_on median 1.0 s (code), then held for the rest of a 10 to 15 s shot.
loom_notes: Draw-on and labels exist; bracket, protractor and ruler shapes are small builders to add.

name: Swap the subject for a familiar object to scale it
description: An extreme value is made relatable by cross-dissolving the subject into a familiar object with a written multiplier, or by placing a tiny human or a hand beside it, then dissolving back so the subject stays the topic.
when_to_use: Extreme sizes, amounts, temperatures or doses.
how_to_execute: Hold the abstract subject on a cool field.
Cross-dissolve to the familiar object on the comparison word.
Write the multiplier beside it.
Dissolve back.
timing: transform_into median 1.0 s (code); the swap can hold through a 15.8 s shot.
loom_notes: Object families plus dissolve exist; household objects beyond the list need assets. The comparison figure must come from the source.

name: Metaphor morphs into the real thing through a shared outline
description: A simple metaphor (a streamlined bird, a vector diagram, a hand-driven wheel) is aligned on the same axis and scale as the real machine and morphs into it through a shared outline or a wireframe, keeping the principle overlay, so the idea transfers.
when_to_use: Analogies that explain a design principle; moving a 2D rule into a 3D device.
how_to_execute: Align metaphor and machine on the same axis and scale.
Show the principle on the metaphor first (flow lines, arrows).
Dissolve through a wireframe into the solid machine, keeping the principle overlay.
Keep identical arrow geometry when going from 2D to 3D.
timing: Metaphor shot about 9.4 s then machine 6.4 s; one combined shot 16.4 s.
loom_notes: Needs a true shape morph and a 2D-to-3D handoff between the SVG runtime and a three.js clip; a matched-outline cross-dissolve is the available substitute.

name: Real photo as a card, annotated by hand
description: Archival or real photos are placed as cards with a soft shadow on a dark textured surface or in a flat frame, then marked with one drawn circle, arrow, measurement or pointing hand as the subject is named.
when_to_use: Grounding a claim in real evidence: case studies, history, the client's own photos.
how_to_execute: Place the photo as a card with a soft shadow on a dark stage or in a frame.
Draw one warm circle or arrow on the subject as it is named.
Write the name in the lesson's label face.
Slide the card out as the next arrives.
timing: Card shots 4 to 11 s.
loom_notes: Needs an image layer and photos from the source (client or public domain); annotation draw-on exists. Grounding rule: never use a photo the source does not supply.

name: Camera arcs up and over to an overhead view
description: The camera swings around and up from eye level beside the subject to an overhead view in one continuous move, revealing the shape of a journey or a city.
when_to_use: Closing reveals and journeys where the layout matters.
how_to_execute: Start at eye level beside the subject.
Arc the camera up and over in one continuous eased move.
Land overhead with the path visible.
timing: One arc of 2.8 s.
loom_notes: Needs a 3D camera; possible only inside a three.js clip.

name: Morph a detailed picture into a flat silhouette to define its parts
description: At the switch from story to definition, the detailed illustration morphs into a flat single-colour silhouette while its colours drain, so one internal part can be filled with the accent and named with a thin pointer label.
when_to_use: The moment a film shifts from story to the definition of a structure.
how_to_execute: Hold the detailed illustration.
Morph its outline to a flat silhouette while the colours drain.
Fill the named region with the accent.
Fade the label in with a thin pointer line on the spoken name, then fade it out.
timing: Morph about 1 s (batch morph median 1.17 s); labels fade in median 0.54 s and out median 0.38 s; whole beat about 7 s.
loom_notes: The colour drain and labelled callouts exist; the shape-to-shape morph does not. A cross-fade from detail to a matching silhouette layer is a reachable approximation when both are drawn on the same geometry.

name: One unit triggers its neighbours into a grid
description: One unit fires and emits a wave that triggers its neighbours, which fire in turn, building a column and then a grid, so exponential growth is visible at a glance.
when_to_use: Cascades, amplification, viral spread, one trigger reaching many.
how_to_execute: Show one unit at rest; change its face or glow when it fires.
Draw a wave from it to two neighbours.
Repeat in staggered rounds until the grid fills.
Hold the full grid.
timing: cmO2ryQ8LcY s029 builds over 16 s.
loom_notes: Staggered groups with seeded arrays cover it.

name: Viewer surrogate parked at the frame edge
description: A flat figure seen from behind or in profile, cropped at a side edge, looks at the framed subject, giving the viewer a shared point of view and steering the eye with its gaze line.
when_to_use: Gallery or museum-wall treatments, product tours, any look-at-this beat.
how_to_execute: Place the figure at a side edge, cropped, facing inward.
Give it one saturated colour so it reads but stays secondary.
Use its gaze line to point at the subject.
Push in past it to isolate the subject when the detail is named.
timing: Present through multi-shot sequences.
loom_notes: Rig characters with poses exist; a back-view pose needs the rig's turnaround.

name: Flat-lay desk as a stage
description: A top-down desk with real props pushed to the edges leaves an empty centre where paper notes swap or new subjects slide in, each paired with a tiny diagram; a slow pan moves between stations.
when_to_use: Research, evidence and source framing; walking through a list of facts as notes.
how_to_execute: Build a top-down desk with props at the frame edges.
Slide or swap one paper note into the empty centre per fact.
Pan slowly to the next note.
Pair each note with a tiny diagram.
timing: Desk pans of 7.6 to 18 s.
loom_notes: The overhead shot size and pan exist, but there is no desk flat-lay place; needs a set and paper-note objects.

name: Backstory told as framed artefacts
description: The past is rendered as artefacts: two-colour bordered pottery-style panels with grain floating in a black void that the camera trucks across, or a historical person inside a gilt frame on a flat warm field who comes alive to gesture.
when_to_use: Backstory, history, the old way, founders.
how_to_execute: Switch to a black void or a flat warm field.
Present the past as a bordered panel or framed portrait with light grain and scratches.
Truck slowly across the panels so the move is the join.
Animate one figure inside the frame for life.
timing: Trucks of about 5 to 6 s per panel.
loom_notes: Paper texture and camera trucks exist; needs panel and frame templates and period artwork.

name: Live speaker annotated with flat graphics
description: Talking-head footage is graded or duotone-tinted toward the flat palette, held as a locked centred medium shot, and annotated by flat badges, keywords and small drawn stand-ins that pop on the spoken term, between short flat cutaways.
when_to_use: Interview or expert-led lessons that use a client's own footage.
how_to_execute: Grade or tint the footage toward the pack palette.
Hold a locked, centred medium shot for the full statement.
Pop a name badge on the name and remove it after.
Pop a keyword or small drawing on the metaphor word.
Cut to 2 to 4 s flat cutaways between holds.
timing: Talking-head holds of 11 to 18 s between 2 to 4 s flat cutaways.
loom_notes: Loom has no footage layer. Needs client footage, a video layer and a duotone shader; badges and pops exist. Grounding: footage must be the client's own.

name: One dot field as the medium every picture forms from
description: A full-frame halftone dot grid is the universal material: portraits, objects and diagrams condense out of it by raising dot density and saturation inside a target shape, then dissolve back into it, so unrelated pictures join without a cut.
when_to_use: Films that move between people, objects and abstract diagrams and need one connective material.
how_to_execute: Lay a full-frame halftone field as the base layer.
Raise dot density and saturation inside a target shape to form the subject.
Draw line details on top once the shape reads.
Dissolve back into the field and form the next subject from it.
timing: Formation beats inside 3.4 to 13.4 s shots; particle motion median about 1.0 s.
loom_notes: Particles exist, but sampling a target shape into dot density (and back) is a new builder. Seen in one film only; kept because the idea of one connective medium is reusable.

name: Same silhouette, new colours for each variant
description: A series of variants or types is shown by hard-cutting the same silhouette with a new body palette and a swapped field colour while pose and head position stay fixed, so variety reads with no new drawings.
when_to_use: Showing many kinds of one thing quickly.
how_to_execute: Draw one silhouette once.
For each variant swap body palette, markings and field colour together.
Keep pose and head position constant.
Cut on each spoken name in a fast burst.
timing: Each variant shot 0.6 to 1.6 s.
loom_notes: Seeded arrays and object states can recolour one shape; hard cuts between stations exist.

name: Radial wedge fan as spotlight, then wipe
description: A full-frame fan of coloured wedges snaps open converging on a subject as a built-in spotlight, drifts during the hold, then the same fan wipes to the next scene.
when_to_use: Introducing one important person or product without text.
how_to_execute: Snap the wedges from a closed point to a full fan.
Hold the subject still on a bright floor band.
Drift the wedges slowly during the hold.
Reuse the fan as the wipe out.
timing: Snap open well under 1 s; hold about 6 s.
loom_notes: A shape or shader preset for the wedge fan and a matching wipe; not present.
